title: Bipartisan duo wants to remind Congress, Trump of China's 'atrocities' ahead of Xi visit
summary: Senators James Lankford and Angus King detail 105 years of Chinese Communist Party repression, from mass killings to Uyghur Muslim detention camps.
story: Fox News senior White House correspondent Peter Doocy reports from the White House as President Donald Trump prepares to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping in a closely watched summit.

FIRST ON FOX: As President Donald Trump readies for a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping Thursday, some lawmakers want to remind the public of the several brutal acts the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) has committed since its founding over a century ago.

Senators James Lankford, R-Okla., and Angus King, I-Maine, have joined forces to push a reminder of a long list of actions obtained by Fox News Digital undertaken by the CCP in pursuit of its "tyrannical ambitions" to grab ahold of and maintain power in China.

Both lawmakers want to put the "countless lives the Chinese Communist Party has destroyed and the people currently living in fear" at the forefront as Trump and Xi prepare for days of talks. And it comes as the CCP celebrates its 105th anniversary since its founding.
GOP CRACKS WIDEN OVER IRAN WAR AS VULNERABLE CANDIDATES BREAK WITH TRUMP, DEMAND ITS END
China's President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump visit the Temple of Heaven May 14, 2026, in Beijing. (Brendan Smialowski/Pool/Getty Images)
"For 105 years, the Chinese Communist Party has oppressed its own people, persecuted people of faith and denied basic freedoms," Lankford said in a statement to Fox News Digital.

"As the United States engages with Beijing, we cannot forget the millions who have suffered under the CCP or those who continue to live under its repression today," he continued. "The United States must continue to stand for religious freedom, human rights and the dignity of every person."
Lankford and King’s resolution lists several instances over the last century when the CCP and its leaders have slain their own citizens, imprisoned dissidents and crushed opposition.
WOMAN WHO SPENT 7 YEARS IN CHINESE PRISON DESCRIBES TORTURE, SURVEILLANCE AND LOSS OF HER HUSBAND

Many happened during the CCP’s push for control, which left a wake of blood and carnage, during the vicious period when People’s Republic of China’s founder Mao Zedong was on the rise during and after World War II and up to the 1960s.

During that period, there was the Yan’an Rectification Movement from 1942 to 1945, when "more than 10,000 people were killed" as the CCP purged dissidents of the movement, and the Chinese Land Reform movement of 1949 to 1953, when between 200,000 and 5 million were slain as the party redistributed rural property to peasantry.
MOTHER RECOUNTS HORRORS OF BRUTAL CHINESE DETENTION CAMP WHERE INFANT SON DIED

Then came the Campaign to Suppress Counterrevolutionaries from 1950 to 1952, with millions of arrests, imprisonments and over 700,000 executions. During that same stretch was the Three-Anti Campaign and the Five-Anti Campaign, when Zedong and the CCP "humiliated, terrorized, exiled, imprisoned, and killed thousands of political opponents and capitalists."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

And, in the last three decades, the resolution noted, the CCP’s iron fist hasn’t loosened its grip, like undermining Hong Kong’s autonomy, targeting religions with "insidious tools of repression" and subjecting an estimated 1 million Uyghur Muslims to "mass detention and torture" in so-called reeducation camps.

Trump will welcome Jinping at Joint Base Andrews Wednesday afternoon, teeing up meetings that are set to last until Friday. Lawmakers are hoping that Trump plays a strong hand during his meetings with Jinping and are urging him to strike trade deals and an agreement on the artificial intelligence race, among other top priorities.
Alex Miller is a writer for Fox News Digital covering the U.S. Senate.

title: Paxton’s estranged wife breaks silence on Texas Senate race after 'biblical grounds' divorce
summary: Angela Paxton urged GOP voters to back Ken Paxton's Texas Senate bid despite their divorce, saying the party seat matters more than personal grievances.
story: Texas GOP U.S. Senate nominee Ken Paxton discusses the impact of the 2026 RNC midterm convention and his Democratic opponent James Talarico seemingly distancing himself from past views on ‘Hannity.’
After filing for divorce on "biblical grounds," Texas Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton’s estranged wife, state Sen. Angela Paxton, addressed whether she would support him this November.
In an address to the Texas Federation of Republican Women themed "the elephant in the room," the state senator stressed that "it’s not the people, it’s the seat."
"We have more control over that seat and the future when we control the seat, when it’s still in the family, even if we’re mad at them," she said as the audience chuckled.
Video of the address was posted on Facebook on Friday by the DeWitt County, Texas, GOP and state Republican Executive Committee member Cheryl Thompson-Draper.
FOX NEWS POLL: GOP DIVISIONS SHAPE TEXAS SENATE RACE

Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton and his wife, state Sen. Angela Paxton, outside the Supreme Court after the court heard two challenges to Texas’ new abortion law on Nov. 1, 2021. State Sen. Paxton filed for divorce last year, citing "biblical grounds." (Bill Clark/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images; David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

This is the first time Paxton’s estranged wife has publicly addressed the Texas Senate race since filing for divorce. Democrats are targeting the seat as they seek to win control of the Senate. Democratic candidate James Talarico held a 3-point edge over Paxton, 51% to 48%, in the most recent Fox News poll. Fox News has categorized the race as a toss-up.

The state senator filed for divorce from Paxton in July 2025. In her filing, Paxton said that her husband had "committed adultery" and that their marriage had "become insupportable because of discord or conflict of personalities."
In a social media post, she wrote that "after 38 years of marriage, I filed for divorce on biblical grounds."

"I believe marriage is a sacred covenant and I have earnestly pursued reconciliation," she added. "But in light of recent discoveries, I do not believe that it honors God or is loving to myself, my children, or Ken to remain in the marriage."
Despite the divorce, the state senator urged GOP voters to remain loyal to the party in this midterm election.
"If we lose it to the other team, the nuances that we want to fix with maybe a certain candidate are nothing compared to what it’s going to take to get it back," she said.
12 RACES SCRAMBLE SENATE BATTLEFIELD AS DEMOCRATS EYE COMEBACK
(Sam Hodde for The Washington Post via Getty Images) (Sam Hodde for The Washington Post via Getty Images)
She acknowledged that personal frustrations with a candidate may influence some voters but emphasized that "when you vote for the person, the party comes along with them."

"The party comes with the person," she continued. "So, when you vote for that person because you like this one better or whatever, you just need to understand, they are not alone, like a standalone thing, like a menu item, you get the whole thing, and we have more control when it’s our party. We have more ability to influence when that person is attached to our party."
Fox News Digital reached out to the state senator, Paxton and Talarico for comment.
After a bruising primary race in which he toppled longtime Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, Paxton has struggled to find his footing in the general election against Talarico.

Even so, Paxton has projected confidence that voters will reject Talarico as a "fake" moderate, pointing to past comments by Talarico, including saying "God is nonbinary" and saying there are six sexes. Paxton has the support of President Donald Trump and financial backing from the president’s MAGA Inc. political action committee as well as Elon Musk’s America PAC.
TALARICO HIT WITH ‘BLATANT CORRUPTION’ ALLEGATION OVER HEFTY SALARY FROM CONSULTING FIRM, CAMPAIGN PUSHES BACK

Left: Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico speaks during a press conference at the Hyatt Centric Congress Avenue on July 22, 2026, in Austin, Texas. Right: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton waves at the conclusion of a campaign event at Matt's Rancho Martinez restaurant on August 4, 2026, in Allen, Texas. (Brandon Bell/Getty Images; Brandon Bell/Getty Images)
In an interview with Fox News earlier this month, Talarico walked back his comments about God being nonbinary and there being six sexes, saying his statements "missed the mark."

In the same interview, however, Talarico said, "I am proud of my legislative track record delivering for Texans."

"I brought Democrats and Republicans together to pass 60 bipartisan bills that lower people’s costs and get the economy back on track," he said, adding, "I'll put my record up against Ken Paxton’s every day of the week and twice on Sunday."
Peter Pinedo is a politics writer for Fox News Digital.

title: Susan Collins tears into bribery allegations as new claims emerge during critical Senate battle
summary: Maine Sen. Susan Collins dismissed the FBI bribery probe as a "political hit job," questioning convicted fraudster Martin Kao's credibility.
story: Fox News contributor Marc Thiessen analyzes the Democratic scramble for a new Maine Senate candidate after Graham Platner's withdrawal amid assault allegations. Thiessen notes the importance of finding a viable candidate to challenge Susan Collins.

Maine Sen. Susan Collins, a Republican, is addressing claims she was caught up in an FBI bribery investigation, dismissing reporting on the story as the work of Democratic operatives and a known conman.

ProPublica reported that Martin Kao, a former defense contractor CEO and convicted fraudster, told the FBI his company funneled $150,000 through a shell company to a super PAC supporting Collins’ 2020 reelection as part of what he described as a broader pay-to-play operation involving political contributions and government contracts. His cooperation later helped open a new phase of the federal investigation that developed into a broader bribery probe.
Shortly after the story broke, Collins spoke up to dismiss Kao on the basis of his character and called into question the origins of the story.

"I've got to say, I do not understand how anyone would take the word of a felon who's been convicted twice — twice, two separate cases — of five counts of money laundering, counts of bank fraud, false submissions to the FEC. He is a convicted liar," the senator told The Wall Street Journal’s Kim Strassel.
GOP SENATOR ALLEGES SCHUMER BEHIND 'HIT JOB' REPORT ON FORMER PATIENTS
U.S. Sen. Susan Collins, R-Maine, walks through the Capitol Jan. 26, 2026, in Washington, D.C. (Heather Diehl/Getty Images)

In a separate interview with Punchbowl News, Collins blamed Democrats and Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer for the controversy, calling the report a "political hit job" and questioning its timing.

Collins is embroiled in a heated re-election campaign against Democrat Troy Jackson. Whether Collins keeps her seat could prove crucial to determining which party controls the Senate in 2027. Any hint of controversy for either candidate, naturally, is suited to become a national controversy.
FOX NEWS POLL: MAINE SENATE RACE IS TIGHT, WITH CONCERNS ABOUT BOTH CANDIDATES
Sen. Susan Collins, R-Maine, departs the chamber at the Capitol in Washington, July 24, 2025. (J. Scott Applewhite/AP Photo)

Campaign finance records cited by ProPublica show that a shell company established by Kao made a donation to a super PAC supporting Collins’ 2020 re-election campaign. The outlet also obtained emails that it says show Scott Reed, head of the super PAC backing Collins that cycle, was aware of the fact that Kao had used a shell company to mask his illegal donation.

A 2019 email from a naval officer shows that the senator had advocated on behalf of Navatek, the contractor Kao was leading at the time. The email, however, was sent months before Kao routed his illegal donation to Collins’ super PAC. Federal contractors are barred from donating to political campaigns, which is why Kao resorted to a shell company.

FBI spokesman Ben Williamson told ProPublica the agency had investigated claims against Collins years ago "and ultimately found nothing implicating Senator Collins or Senator Collins’ campaign. Any suggestion otherwise is totally false."

The FBI, however, did not respond to ProPublica’s questions about a new investigation it says was launched in 2024 after Kao spent years cooperating with federal agents and detailing his dealings with Collins and other lawmakers.

"The Biden-led Justice Department and FBI totally cleared my office, my campaign and me five years ago of these 7-year-old allegations," Collins said, also not addressing the 2024 investigation directly.
GOP SENATOR ALLEGES SCHUMER BEHIND 'HIT JOB' REPORT ON FORMER PATIENTS
Sen. Susan Collins, R-Maine, arrives for a Republican luncheon at the U.S. Capitol Feb. 20, 2025, in Washington, D.C. (Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images)

Kao had a clear incentive to cooperate with the FBI. He was facing years in prison and hoped that providing information would help reduce his sentence, although the judge ultimately gave him no leniency for his cooperation.

"This is a smear job. And as someone who has always prided herself on serving with integrity, it really offends me," Collins said. "And I'm offended for my staff too, both on the campaign and in the personal office."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Collins’ office did not return a request for comment when reached by Fox News Digital on Wednesday.

title: Mamdani roasted for staying tight-lipped on 'war criminal' Pezeshkian after raging about Netanyahu
summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani called Benjamin Netanyahu a war criminal but faces backlash for silence on Iran's Masoud Pezeshkian at UNGA.
story: Fox News correspondent Alexis McAdams reports on New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani calling for the arrest of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ahead of his visit to the United Nations. Israeli Ambassador to the U.N. Danny Danon joins 'America Reports' to react to the controversial comments and discuss the threat of Iran-backed attacks against regional allies.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani repeatedly branded Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu a "war criminal," but faced criticism for remaining largely tight-lipped about Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian’s visit to New York for the United Nations General Assembly.

While Mamdani has labeled the Iranian government "brutal" and cited its "systematic repression of its own people," critics railed against him for declining to use similar language about Pezeshkian, who arrived in the city on Wednesday.

"Mayor Mamdani, you said war criminals who set foot in New York should be arrested. Good news. One is in New York city this week," said Iranian-born journalist Masih Alinejad, who was subjected to an assassination attempt near her Brooklyn home while Ayatollah Ali Hosseini Khamenei was still alive.
"If you have the courage to talk about arresting those responsible for crimes against humanity, start with the man sleeping five miles from your office," Alinejad tweeted.
TRUMP, IRANIAN PRESIDENT CONVERGE ON NYC FOR ‘DRAMATIC’ UN SHOWDOWN AS TEHRAN FACES TIGHT RESTRICTIONS

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani branded Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu a "war criminal" and urged the federal government to arrest him under an International Criminal Court warrant on July 21, 2026. ((L) Reuters, (R) @NYCMayor via X)
She invited Mamdani to view the FBI files about her case, in which several men attempted to kidnap her in Brooklyn.

Director of National Intelligence Walter "Jay" Clayton said in January that the Iranian regime coordinated a murder-for-hire plot against Alinejad because of her efforts to speak out against its human rights abuses, while federal authorities sentenced one U.S.-based conspirator to 15 years.

"The government of Iran, a sponsor of terrorism, assassination, and espionage around the globe, has engaged in a campaign of assassination plots in the United States and abroad targeting those who oppose the regime," Clayton said in a statement.
MAMDANI MAKES EYEBROW-RAISING CLAIM ABOUT NETANYAHU PROTESTS AHEAD OF NYC VISIT

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian speaks during celebrations marking the 46th anniversary of the 1979 Islamic revolution in Tehran, Iran, on Feb. 10, 2025. (Iranian Presidency/Anadolu via Getty Images)
Meanwhile, Mamdani has said Netanyahu is not welcome in New York City and has called him an "architect" of "genocide." No similar statements about Pezeshkian could be found.
Fox News Digital reached out to Mamdani for comment.
National security expert and ACT For America founder Brigitte Gabriel also criticized the mayor over the discrepancy.
Gabriel, who has said she survived a terror attack during the 1975 Lebanese Civil War in Lebanon, now lives in the U.S.

"[The] Iranian President on American soil — while we are still in open conflict with Iran. 18 Americans dead. Thousands of Iranians slaughtered. And he’s getting a visa, a hotel, and a UN microphone in New York," Gabriel fumed on X.
"Where are the war crimes charges? Where’s Mamdani to arrest him while he’s in NYC?"
ISRAEL'S AMBASSADOR SAYS NYC’S MAMDANI IS ‘SOWING CHAOS’ AHEAD OF NETANYAHU’S UN APPEARANCE
Masih Alinejad, a prominent Iranian American human rights activist, attends an interview with the Associated Press in Berlin, Germany, on Nov. 9, 2024. (AP Photo/Ebrahim Noroozi, File)
Israeli U.N. Ambassador Danny Danon told reporters Tuesday that Mamdani should stop attacking his nation’s government and turn his attention to Pezeshkian’s administration.
"Focus on the problems of the City of New York and stop with promoting anti-Semitism, stop supporting Hamas, and stop engaging with the Iranian regime," Danon said.
Those comments came weeks after Mamdani’s international affairs liaison sought to arrange a meeting with Iranian U.N. Ambassador Amir-Saeid Iravani.
Senate Intelligence Committee Chairman Tom Cotton told Fox News the disparity in Mamdani’s rhetoric is stark.
TRUMP TO MEET WITH MAMDANI IN NEW YORK AMID HIGH-STAKES MIDTERM PUSH
"Is Zohran Mamdani threatening to arrest butchers from Iran who have killed tens of thousands of their own people, or genuine war criminals from other countries?" Cotton, R-Ark., asked.

President Donald Trump and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani meet at Gracie Mansion on Sept. 21, 2026.
"No. The one person he cites is the leader of the Jewish State of Israel."

While Mamdani met with President Donald Trump on Tuesday, he said afterward the two leaders will continue to have radically different views on Israel and the conflict in Iran.

title: Melania Trump reveals 'the world's biggest untapped economic force' to kick off landmark NYSE summit
summary: Melania Trump rang the opening bell at the New York Stock Exchange and urged female CEOs to move beyond mentorship toward ownership at IMPERIA.
story: Speaking at the New York Stock Exchange, an address outlines why women represent the ultimate untapped economic force in the global marketplace. The speech emphasizes that the next chapter of economic progress relies on women owning businesses, capital, and intellectual property. Without women as consumers, investors, and leaders, the modern economy would fracture under severe shocks.
First lady Melania Trump touted the outsized role women play in the American and global economies during a keynote speech at the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) on Wednesday.

"People still do not fully understand the full scale of women's power in the global economy. Women are not just a part of [the] marketplace, simple participants," she said while speaking at IMPERIA, the first invite-only global summit at the NYSE designed exclusively for female CEOs and executives.
"We are its foundation and we are its infrastructure," she continued.
FIRST LADY MELANIA TRUMP, FOX CORPORATION ANNOUNCE LANDMARK STRATEGIC ALLIANCE TO GROW FOSTERING THE FUTURE
Ringing in the morning bell at the exchange, Trump also made the case that women remain a latent asset in the marketplace.
First lady Melania Trump, with Lynn Martin, president of NYSE Group, signs the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) guestbook, after ringing the opening bell, Sept. 23, 2026. (Reuters/Brendan McDermid)
"The world's biggest untapped economic force is not a new market, a breakthrough technology or an undiscovered natural resource. It is women coming together as owners," the first lady said.
She then painted a picture of what the market would look like absent the driving force of female impact.
"Remove women as consumers, investors, leaders, caregivers, innovators and managers of household finances and the modern economy would not work as it does today," she said.

"Remove women from the workforce and we would lose doctors, engineers, bankers, lawyers and millions of other professionals. Remove women from the unseen and ignored economy of care, childcare, running households, home teaching and caring for elderly or sick family members and the support structure that lets others work for pay begins to collapse. Remove women from capital formation and we lose investors, shareholders, asset managers, property owners, retirement savers and those who protect intergenerational wealth," Trump continued.
First lady Melania Trump greets people after ringing the New York Stock Exchange opening bell, Sept. 23, 2026. (Reuters/Brendan McDermid)
The first lady then closed with a plea for the world, and especially the women present, to invest more in women.
SEN DAVE MCCORMICK: TRUMP ACCOUNTS GIVE ALL AMERICANS A STAKE IN PROSPERITY

"Together, we can convert individual success into collective momentum to create new opportunities, support each other's growth and drive lasting economic power. Now is our time to move beyond mentorship and toward ownership. Do not simply advise another woman. Invest in her. Do not merely open a door. Create a real opportunity," she said.

"Turn networks into tangible value capital. Customers, contracts, knowledge and success. Be intentional with your purchases. Invest in one another. Invite another outstanding woman into the boardroom. Help an entry entrepreneur land the first big customer, fund new ideas that should exist," Trump continued.
First lady Melania Trump signs the New York Stock Exchange guestbook, Sept. 23, 2026. (Reuters/Brendan McDermid)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"The women here have built companies, created wealth and transformed industries. But imagine that power connected before you depart here today. Begin to work with each other. Let's turn this gathering into meaningful action. Women are on the global economy infrastructure. Now let's use that stronghold to own more of it together," she concluded.

title: The top moments from Iran president’s tense visit to US soil as war rages
summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian cast Iran as a victim of U.S. aggression at the United Nations General Assembly as a delegate walked out.
story: Iranian president used his UN General Assembly address to display images of children killed in a strike on a school and accuse the US and Israel of attacks on Iranian civilians. (Credit: UNTV)

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian defended Tehran’s conduct in its war with the United States on Wednesday, taking aim at President Donald Trump and vowing that Iran would not surrender during a fiery address before world leaders at the United Nations General Assembly.

The speech follows months of fighting, failed diplomatic efforts and mounting international pressure on Tehran, giving Pezeshkian a high-profile platform to defend Iran’s actions and challenge the U.S. account of the conflict.

"America and Israel attacked us, equipped with the latest technology and weapons systems, and our people stood steadfast. Yes, they did hit us, but we did not bend the knee. We did not bow our head," said Pezeshkian. "Those who are terrorists and train and protect terrorists describe us as such. We have only defended ourselves. We are not terrorists."
Fox News Digital compiled the top moments from Pezeshkian’s speech and the developments unfolding both inside and outside the U.N.
ONE GLARING ISSUE GOES UNADDRESSED IN UN CHIEF'S HIGH-STAKES TALKS WITH IRAN'S PRESIDENT

Masoud Pezeshkian, Iran's president, during the United Nations General Assembly in New York, US, on Wednesday, Sept. 23, 2026. The theme of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly is "Restoring trust, managing transformation: A United Nations that delivers for all." (John Lamparski/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Pezeshkian’s fiery attacks on Trump and the United States came amid a hostile reception in New York City, where protesters gathered to denounce the Iranian government as its president addressed world leaders at the United Nations.
Former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani joined a "Free Iran" rally outside the U.N., where protesters denounced Tehran as Pezeshkian addressed world leaders.
"Free Iran" protests are held outside the UN during the United Nations General Assembly Wednesday. (Ted Goodman, Goodman & Co)
Demonstrators waved Iranian flags while denouncing Iran’s government over its repression of political dissent, restrictions on women’s rights and treatment of opposition figures.
"Free Iran" protests are held outside the UN during the United Nations General Assembly Wednesday. (Ted Goodman, Goodman & Co)
As the emcee announced Pezeshkian's impending speech, audible boos erupted from the protest crowd outside the UN as the leader walked out onto the stage.
A member of the U.S. delegation walked out of the General Assembly hall after Pezeshkian began criticizing the United States during his speech, Fox News Digital previously reported.
Fox News Digital reached out to the U.S. Mission for comment.
TRUMP DEFENDS US INTERVENTIONS ABROAD AHEAD OF 'BIG DECISION' ON IRAN: 'SETTLING YEARS OF UNFINISHED BUSINESS'
Pezeshkian used his speech to defend Iran’s conduct during the war and take aim at the United States and Israel.
"The United States using weapons with multiple warheads targeted that sports hall. … They martyred, assassinated our scientists, our men, women and children," he said.
"This is what the United States seeks to do with all countries — [to] sacrifice the population of a country in order to achieve [its] goals," Pezeshkian added.

CENTCOM has denied that U.S. forces carried out the strike on the sports hall in Lamerd, saying American forces did not strike the city or anywhere within 30 miles of it on the opening day of Operation Epic Fury.
FIVE TOP TAKEAWAYS FROM TRUMP'S HIGH-STAKES UN SPEECH TO THE WORLD
"Free Iran" protests are held outside the UN during the United Nations General Assembly Wednesday. (Ted Goodman, Goodman & Co)
Pezeshkian said that the U.S. and Israel have learned that Iran cannot be made to surrender, reiterating that Iran is "not afraid of fighting" and would defend the country "until our last breath."
TRUMP WARNS IRAN WILL BE HIT 'REALLY HARD' IF NUCLEAR NEGOTIATIONS COLLAPSE AGAIN
During a moment of his speech, Pezeshkian held up props showing photos of the late Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and Iranian schoolchildren killed during the beginning of the conflict.

Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian speaks as he holds a picture of Ali Khamenei, former Supreme Leader of Iran, during the 81st United Nations General Assembly at the United Nations Headquarters in New York, on September 23, 2026. (TIMOTHY A. CLARY / AFP via Getty Images)

"Our innocent people have been the targets of cowardly attacks and aggressions imposed upon our country. And we defended ourselves with utmost strength. America and Israel attacked us," Pezeshkian said.
He also used the opportunity to take shots at Trump, accusing him of "bullying" Iran.
"More must be understood by Mr. Trump and those who seek to bully us, that we are ready for dialog and diplomacy and negotiations without accepting the language of force," Pezeshkian said.

Trump addressed leaders Tuesday and said he faced a "big decision" between reaching a deal with Iran or, in his words, "annihilat[ing] the Islamic Republic," before U.S. officials later met with Iranian officials.

"Going back to the words of the president of the United States yesterday … everything uttered about our country was against the very essence and charter in the spirit of the United Nations," Pezeshkian said. "He must know that the resistance of the Iranian people will increase in the face of sanctions, and increased bullying, because all of us under law will never bow our head or bend at the knee."
Administration officials quickly pushed back on Pezeshkian’s attacks and disputed his account of the conflict.

"I think sponsoring terrorist organizations in the region to attack your neighbors, attack energy infrastructure, attack civilian sites is a violation of the UN system. So I don't know what's standing. Iran has to lecture anyone on human rights or the international system. When they habitually violate it," said Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
Rubio added that Iran has no credibility defending the international order because its regime has repeatedly violated it.

"The Iranian regime has murdered thousands of its own people, killed Americans overseas, executed acts of terrorism in the Strait of Hormuz, and launched indiscriminate attacks against its neighbors in the region," White House deputy press secretary Anna Kelly told Fox News Digital.
"The President is courageously ensuring that such an evil country never possesses a nuclear weapon, which will make the entire world safer and more stable," she added.
Ashley J. DiMella reports on politics for Fox News Digital.

title: Supreme Court to hear Missouri redistricting case for third time
summary: Justice Brett Kavanaugh accepted an emergency appeal in the Missouri redistricting case as the 2025 map faces its third Supreme Court review.
story: Fox News correspondent Mark Meredith has the latest on the key storylines shaping the race to the 2026 midterm elections, including the political fallout from the Supreme Court's Missouri redistricting decision, the battle for control of Congress, and the issues driving voters as both parties intensify their push toward November on 'Special Report.'
The U.S. Supreme Court will hear arguments in a Missouri redistricting case for a third time after Justice Brett Kavanaugh accepted a request to intervene in the case once again Tuesday night.

The divisive redistricting map drawn in 2025 would grant Republicans an additional seat in the House of Representatives if it is put in place ahead of the 2026 elections. A federal judge in Missouri ruled in favor of the 2025 map last month, but the Supreme Court put a stay on that ruling just two weeks ago.
Opponents of the map issued an emergency appeal to the Supreme Court late Tuesday night after the St. Louis-based Eighth U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals ruled in favor of the new map on Monday.
FEDERAL APPEALS COURT ORDERS MISSOURI TO USE CONGRESSIONAL MAP REJECTED TWICE BY SUPREME COURT

The maps show how Missouri’s congressional districts changed between 2022 and 2025, including the expansion of the Kansas City-area 5th District into more Republican-leaning rural parts of the state. (Missouri Office of Administration/Amanda Macias/Fox News Digital)
Kavanaugh handles emergency requests for the state of Missouri and directed supporters of the new map to respond to the appeal by Wednesday at 2 p.m. ET.

The development is the latest in a roller-coaster ride of legal decisions that have seen the new map fly up and down between federal and state courts, the Supreme Court and the Missouri Supreme Court.
ELECTION CHAOS IN THIS RED STATE JUST GOT EVEN STRANGER FOR REPUBLICANS AFTER SUPREME COURT RULING

The case began when Missouri Secretary of State Denny Hoskins rejected a petition for the 2025 map to be placed on the ballot for a vote in 2026. Instead, the new map was used to determine congressional districts for the state's primary elections.

People gather at the Missouri statehouse in Jefferson City on Sept. 10, 2025, to protest changes to the state's congressional district maps. (Tammy Ljungblad/Kansas City Star/Tribune News Service via Getty Images)

The Democratic group behind the petition, People Not Politicians, asked a state court to intervene, saying the group's petition of 300,000 signatures should have triggered a referendum on the new map under Missouri's constitution. The Missouri Supreme Court agreed, writing that the 2025 map cannot go into effect "unless and until approved by the voters at the November 2026 general election."
MISSOURI HIGH COURT BLOCKS GOP-BACKED CONGRESSIONAL MAPS AHEAD OF MIDTERMS; TRUMP BLASTS 'RIDICULOUS' RULING
Hoskins then appealed the case to the Supreme Court, but Kavanaugh declined to hear his request on Sept. 4.

Meanwhile, Republican candidates who won primary elections based on the 2025 maps brought up a separate case in federal court, arguing that if the general election takes place under the 2022 map their districts would be very different from the primary maps. Many general election voters, they noted, would also be presented with options they had no role in voting for during the primaries.
SUPREME COURT AGAIN BLOCKS MISSOURI FROM USING TRUMP-BACKED CONGRESSIONAL MAPS
Missouri's high court blocked the new redistricting map and ordered a statewide vote in November on whether to keep it. (AP Photo/David A. Lieb)

Eighth Circuit Judge Stephen R. Clark ruled in favor of those candidates and issued an order requiring that the 2025 maps be used in this year's elections, effectively contradicting the state Supreme Court.

This time, People Not Politicians asked the U.S. Supreme Court to intervene, and Kavanaugh agreed. The court issued an unsigned order blocking Clark's order until the Eighth Circuit issued a formal ruling in the case. The Eighth Circuit then fast-tracked the case and ruled in favor of the 2025 map.
MISSOURI SUPREME COURT THREATENS SECRETARY OF STATE WITH CONTEMPT AMID INTENSIFYING REDISTRICTING BATTLE

People Not Politicians filed their latest request for an intervention on Tuesday night, arguing that the court's ruling against the new map was still in effect, and pointing to statements from Missouri election officials saying it is too late to change what maps are used in the upcoming elections.
Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh speaks at his Senate confirmation hearing on Capitol Hill, Sept. 27, 2018. (Michael Reynolds-Pool/Getty Images)

The Missouri Association of County Clerks and Election Authorities already announced it will not be using the 2025 map for November, arguing in an appeal filing that the state does not have enough time to provide new ballots.

"Ballots have been printed, and Missourians have already voted. Thousands more will vote before this order seeks to take effect. Officials should stop wasting taxpayers’ money on pointless legal action and instead focus on administering our elections," People Not Politicians director Richard von Glahn said in a statement.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.
Anders Hagstrom is a reporter with Fox News Digital covering national politics and major breaking news events.

title: Trump to ask Xi to free wrongfully detained US citizen as wife speaks out
summary: President Trump plans to ask Chinese President Xi Jinping to release Dr. Youlin Chen, a U.S. citizen charged with espionage after two years in China.
story: Wives of Americans wrongfully detained in China appeal for their husbands' release ahead of a high-stakes meeting between President Donald Trump and Xi Jinping. Gillian Turner reports on the families of Youlin Chen and Min Zin as they share their emotional struggles and express hope for diplomatic intervention during bilateral discussions.

President Donald Trump plans to ask Chinese President Xi Jinping to release wrongfully detained U.S. citizen Dr. Youlin Chen, the man's family told Fox News after his wife and the wife of another detainee spoke exclusively to "Fox & Friends" Wednesday.
The wives of two wrongfully detained Americans in China made a plea for Trump to intervene in their husbands' detention during an interview with Fox News senior foreign correspondent Gillian Turner.

Yugang Rong and Sylvia Zin implored Trump to intervene in the cases of their husbands, Chen, a seismic and nuclear researcher, and Min Zin, a scholar with a focus on Myanmar, respectively. The pair are the only two U.S. citizens in China that have been designated by the U.S. State Department as wrongfully detained.
CHINA’S XI SET TO ARRIVE IN WASHINGTON FOR HIGH-STAKES TRUMP SUMMIT AS AI SUPREMACY BATTLE LOOMS LARGE
"My husband is an American citizen. He is the father of my son and we terribly miss him," Rong told Turner.
Chen was taken from outside the Beijing airport by Chinese agents in November 2024, according to a website dedicated to his release.
A headshot of Dr. Youlin Chen, courtesy of the James W. Foley Legacy Foundation. (James W. Foley Legacy Foundation.)
After Chinese agents took him, they reportedly seized his cellphone, iPad, laptop and cameras and repeatedly logged onto his email accounts and accessed his devices.
His wife believes he was taken because of his seismic research into nuclear activity.
"It's his research work. He has been doing a lot of research on how to monitor nuclear tests," she told "Fox & Friends."

His research, according to the website, "focuses on the Earth's crustal structures in Asia using regional earthquake data, including data sourced from and in collaboration with earthquake scientists in China."
In one of his publicly available reports he used geophysical research methods to detect North Korean nuclear tests.

A Japanese news broadcast of a test launch of new intercontinental ballistic missile, the "Hwasong-19," at an undisclosed place in North Korea. North Korea's Korean Central News Agency (KCNA) said on Nov. 1 that it successfully test-fired the missile the previous day. (Jae-Hwan/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)
China charged Chen with espionage, but he has yet to receive a trial despite over two years of imprisonment. He has not been allowed any contact with his family.
DAUGHTER OF DETAINED CHINESE PASTOR SAYS SHE HAS 'HOPE' AFTER LEARNING TRUMP MAY RAISE CASE WITH XI JINPING
Sylvia Zin, meanwhile, does not understand why her husband, whose research focuses on military government and Chinese-Myanmar relations, was taken.

"Unlike Dr. Chen, I really have no idea why, what in his research that they would be interested in. He is an open source researcher, and all of his work is published on their website," Zin told Turner.
MY FATHER IS A PASTOR, IMPRISONED IN CHINA. PRESIDENT TRUMP, PLEASE SAVE HIM
Headshot of Min Zin. (James W. Foley Legacy Foundation.)
Both women made a plea to the president to intervene.
"At this point, I think the president is the only person who can move ahead in this case and bring him home," Zin said.
PASTOR FREED FROM CHINESE PRISON AFTER TRUMP RAISED HIS CASE WITH XI JINPING
Both Zin and Rong said they were hopeful that Trump would bring their husbands home.
"President Trump has done a lot for us. He has personally been involved in this case. I know whenever he [gets] personally involved in cases, Americans come home," Rong said.
US MARINE VETERAN RELEASED FROM RUSSIAN PRISON AFTER 1,666 DAYS OF DETENTION
The Trump administration has succeeded in securing the freedom of 83 U.S. nationals detained abroad in the past year, according to a report from the James W. Foley Legacy Foundation.

Fox News' Gillian Turner contributed to this report.

title: SHOCK POLL: Powerful blue state gov's lead shrinks to single digits weeks before election
summary: Bruce Blakeman trails Kathy Hochul by just nine points in a new Siena poll, closing the gap in a state where Democrats outnumber Republicans two-to-one.
story: Economic policy debates heat up as Kathy Hochul and Bruce Blakeman clash over New York's future. Mike Lee joins the discussion to analyze Siena University poll numbers showing Hochul leading the gubernatorial race. The segment highlights controversial decisions like the statewide data center moratorium and a newly proposed energy rebate program.

Democrats outnumber Republicans by a roughly two-to-one margin in blue-leaning New York State, but a new poll indicates Republican gubernatorial nominee Bruce Blakeman has cut his deficit to Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul to single digits with just six weeks to go until Election Day.

Hochul, who is running for a second full four-year term steering the nation's fourth most populous state, stands at 50% support among likely voters in New York, with Blakeman at 41%, according to a Siena College poll conducted Sept. 11-17 and released on Wednesday.

Blakeman, the Nassau County executive on New York's Long Island, trailed Hochul by 10 points in Siena's August survey. The one-point movement by Blakeman, who is aiming to become the first Republican in nearly a quarter-century to win an election for governor in New York, is within the survey's margin of error.

"With six weeks until election day, voters offer good news to both Hochul and Blakeman. She now has the support of 50% of voters and saw her favorability and job approval ratings edge into positive territory. He now trails by single digits – well, nine points – in a state where Democrats outnumber Republicans by more than two-to-one," Siena pollster Steven Greenberg said.
CHECK OUT THE LATEST FOX NEWS POLLING IN THE MIDTERM ELECTIONS

Nassau County Executive Bruce Blakeman, left, and New York Gov. Kathy Hochul. Blakeman, the GOP gubernatorial nominee, is challenging Hochul, a Democrat, in the 2026 election. (NDZ/Star Max/GC Images/Getty Images; Alexander MacDougall/Albany Times Union via Getty Images)

Greenberg noted that at this point four years ago, Hochul held a 17-point lead over then-Rep. Lee Zeldin, the GOP nominee. But Zeldin closed the gap and ended up losing to Hochul by only six points in the 2022 election.
"Currently, Blakeman is doing a better job with Republicans, leading 88-8%, than Hochul is with Democrats, leading 81-11%," Greenberg added.
The GOP nominee is also edging Hochul 44%-39% among independent voters.

"All polls continue to show Kathy Hochul's downward spiral and me closing the gap as New Yorkers learn more about my plan to cut income taxes by historic margins and slash electric bills in half," Blakeman argued in a statement after the release of the Siena poll.
But the new poll indicates that two-thirds of New York State voters, including 37% of Republicans, think Hochul will win re-election.
Meanwhile, a Quinnipiac University poll also released Wednesday indicated Hochul leading by 19 points, 58% to 39% over Blakeman.
DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB
Bruce Blakeman, Nassau County executive and Republican candidate for New York governor, received President Donald Trump's endorsement earlier this year. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

Blakeman is a strong supporter of President Donald Trump, who in February endorsed his bid for governor. But Trump's support may be doing Blakeman no favors, with half of likely voters, including a quarter of Republicans, saying it's a negative for the GOP nominee's campaign.

Hochul was endorsed earlier this year by New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, the first socialist mayor of the nation's most populous city, reciprocating her backing during his own historic mayoral run last year.
By a 50%-30% margin, voters said Mamdani's support for Hochul is a plus for the governor's bid for re-election.
SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

New York Gov. Kathy Hochul listens as New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani speaks during the annual New York State Financial Control Board meeting on Aug. 12, 2026, in New York City. Mamdani earlier this year endorsed Hochul's re-election bid. (Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)
Then-Lt. Gov. Hochul was sworn in as New York’s first female governor in August 2021 after Gov. Andrew Cuomo, in the middle of his third term, resigned amid multiple scandals.
Hochul has seen her political standing rise over the past year and a half as she's increased her resistance to Trump's unprecedented second-term agenda.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Asked about the poll, Hochul campaign spokesperson Ryan Radulovacki, referring to Blakeman, told Fox News Digital, "No one wants a Trump puppet in the governor’s mansion who will cut their healthcare, raise their costs, and let ICE trample their rights."
"They trust Governor Hochul’s record of investing in public safety, lowering crime, and putting money back in their pockets – and they know she’ll fight for their families, not Trump," he added.

The poll, which was conducted by telephone and text-to-web collection, surveyed 1,144 likely voters in New York, with an overall margin of error of plus or minus 3.9 percentage points for core questions.
Paul Steinhauser covers the national campaign trail from coast to coast for Fox News

title: FIRST ON FOX: Rubio ramps up birth tourism crackdown hours before Xi touches down in US
summary: Marco Rubio announced visa restrictions on those who engage in or facilitate birth tourism as Xi Jinping arrives for a high-stakes state visit.
story: Fox News chief congressional correspondent Chad Pergram reports on a House hearing over alleged birth tourism and birthright citizenship on 'Special Report.'

FIRST ON FOX — Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced Wednesday that the Trump administration is moving to restrict visas to individuals who "engage in or facilitate" birth tourism hours before Chinese President Xi Jinping arrives in the United States for a state visit, Fox News Digital has learned.

"By restricting visa issuance of those who both engage in and profit from this fraud, we are sending a clear message: The United States will not allow foreigners to exploit our immigration system and violate the sanctity of U.S. citizenship," a statement from Rubio obtained by Fox News Digital states.

The restrictions target foreigners who "knowingly engage in, have engaged in, or facilitate birth tourism," including non-citizens who work in the birth tourism industry, so-called fixers who coach visa applicants to commit fraud, as well as others "who support, abet, and enable commercial birth tourism."
BIRTH TOURISM FIGHT SHIFTS TO US ‘TROPICAL MATERNITY WARD’ WITH HISTORY OF CHINESE EXPLOITATION
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced new policies surrounding visas on Wednesday. (Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images)

Birth tourism is the practice of traveling to the United States for the primary purpose of giving birth so the child obtains U.S. citizenship. China has been a particular focus of federal efforts to combat the practice, with Justice Department cases targeting large-scale birth tourism operations catering predominantly to Chinese clients. Chinese nationals have traveled to clinics on the West Coast and to Saipan — part of the U.S. Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands — to give birth.
Rep. Brandon Gill, R-Texas, who chairs a House Oversight task force investigating birth tourism, has also singled out China and Russia in raising concerns about the practice.

China could also stand to gain from a reduction in birth tourism as the country faces a steep demographic decline. Young people leaving for the United States, a process made much easier if they’re already citizens, could exacerbate China's troubles on that front.
TRUMP’S TOUGHER ROUND-TWO BIRTHRIGHT CITIZENSHIP STRATEGY HINGES ON KEY LEGAL DISTINCTION, EXPERTS SAY
Chinese President Xi Jinping, left, shakes hands with U.S. President Donald Trump at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, Thursday, May 14, 2026. (Kenny Holston/Pool Photo via AP)

Cracking down on birth tourism has been a cornerstone of the Trump administration’s immigration agenda. Alongside countering birth tourism, the Trump administration has also unsuccessfully sought to overturn birthright citizenship as part of its push to address what it feels are abuses of the American system.

After the Supreme Court struck down the federal government's initial attempt to do away with birthright citizenship, President Donald Trump issued two follow-up executive orders. One sought to deny citizenship to children born to members of designated terrorist organizations and the other directed the State Department to deny travel visas to or pursue removal actions against individuals believed to be in the country for the purposes of birth tourism.
AMERICA AND CHINA ARE FIGHTING FOR THE FUTURE OF AI — CHIPS ARE THE BATTLEFIELD
Chinese President Xi Jinping, right, and U.S. President Donald Trump meet at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing. (Kenny Holston/Pool Photo via AP)

"The Trump Administration is using every tool at our disposal to defend the integrity of U.S. citizenship, protect American public benefits and U.S. taxpayers from exploitation, and safeguard our national security," Rubio said in his statement.

Xi arrives Wednesday evening for a tense White House summit with Trump covering AI, tariffs, rare earth minerals and fentanyl exports.
Ashley J. DiMella reports on politics for Fox News Digital.

title: GOP cracks widen over Iran war as vulnerable candidates break with Trump, demand its end
summary: Vulnerable Republicans Ashley Hinson, Mike Rogers and Jon Husted break with Trump on the Iran war as gas prices reshape toss-up Senate races.
story: Former Rep. Mike Rogers joined other vulnerable Republicans running for office to call for an immediate end to the Iran war. He told Fox News Digital in Dallas
Vulnerable Republicans running for their political lives have, for months, kept quiet or sided with President Donald Trump on the war in Iran.

But as costs rise and voters pepper them with questions on the campaign trail about when the fighting will end, some are changing their tune and breaking with Trump, arguing the war must end to lower prices — including lawmakers who previously voted to continue the conflict in the Middle East.
Rep. Ashley Hinson, R-Iowa, former Rep. Mike Rogers, R-Mich., and Sen. Jon Husted, R-Ohio, are all running in toss-up races that will define the balance of power in the Senate.
TRUMP-BACKED IOWA US SENATE HOPEFUL SAYS IRAN WAR MUST 'BE BROUGHT TO A SUCCESSFUL AND IMMEDIATE END'
President Donald Trump during the United Nations General Assembly in New York on Tuesday, Sept. 22, 2026. (Bloomberg via Getty Images)

Hinson, whose agriculture-heavy state is getting hit with high diesel costs, argued that lawmakers needed to suspend the gas tax, pause diesel exports, "unleash E-15 everywhere we can," reinstate biodiesel tax credits and create a diesel relief program.
"These actions to lower costs are needed ASAP, and the war needs to be brought to a successful and immediate end," Hinson said.
Her race against Iowa state Rep. Josh Turek is listed as a toss-up, according to the Cook Political Report.

Hinson, however, has voted against every war powers resolution offered in the House. Notably, she voted against the successful war powers resolution when seven House Republicans, including two other Republican members of the Iowa House delegation, voted for it.
FOX NEWS POLL: 71% THINK TRUMP ADMINISTRATION LACKS PLAN TO END IRAN WAR

Rogers has been out of Congress since 2015 but is running in one of the most-watched toss-up races this cycle against Abdul El-Sayed, and Republicans hope to flip a state that eluded them when Trump ran for his second term two years ago.
Shortly after Hinson’s shift in position, he released an ad echoing an immediate end to the war.
But weeks earlier, the former lawmaker, who voted in favor of the war in Iraq in 2002, told Fox News Digital at the GOP’s made-for-TV huddle in Dallas that he wanted to see the war come to an end.
"Well, first of all, I'd like to see this thing come to an end. They need to find a way to get this thing ended," Rogers said. "I think that's certainly where Michigan voters, Michigan families are."
7 REPUBLICANS REBEL AGAINST TRUMP, VOTE WITH DEMS TO REIN IN IRAN WAR POWERS
A semi-truck driver replaces a diesel fuel pump at a Love's gas station in Eloy, Ariz., on March 18, 2026. (Rebecca Noble/Bloomberg via Getty Images)

"Again, I think we have to understand, do we want Iran to have a nuclear weapon? I think most people overwhelmingly say no," he continued. "Would they like this to come to an end? I say absolutely yes."

Husted, who is running in another toss-up contest against former Sen. Sherrod Brown in Ohio, has also pivoted. And like Hinson, he has voted against every war powers resolution that has hit the floor in the Senate.
"The war needs to come to an end as quickly as possible so that we can lower gas prices," Husted told Politico.

Husted, like others, has pushed several times for a "brief and successful" end to the war over the last seven months, and like several Republicans, has made the case that getting the Strait of Hormuz running and open was a paramount goal.
Olivia Tripodi, a spokesperson for Husted, told Fox News Digital that the lawmaker's "position has not changed. Any accusation otherwise has not listened to Sen. Husted over the last seven months."

"Since the beginning of the conflict in Iran, he has called for the military operation to be successful but brief so that gas prices can go down for Ohioans, but that enacting a War Powers Resolution would undermine the U.S. negotiating position and potentially put American troops and allies at risk," Tripodi said. "He has also supported the president’s efforts to negotiate a settlement to end the war, despite the Iranian side’s refusal to negotiate in good faith and its efforts to extend the conflict and bomb U.S. ships."
Some Republican leaders are encouraging candidates to break with Trump to make their own bespoke campaigns, particularly as the war’s unpopularity continues to increase.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., who is crisscrossing the country to rally support and funds for candidates, said he encourages "most candidates to run their own campaigns."

"Well, I mean, I think, you know, if I'm running in an environment like this, you know, obviously, you're gonna develop a campaign and a message that can win in your state. And so, I encourage most candidates to run their own campaigns."

"I mean, obviously, the president's gonna be a factor in every election. It’s a midterm election, he's not on the ballot," Thune said. "But, I mean, obviously, there are gonna be probably policies of his they agree with, and some that they don't. But I think they need to be their own person. And I think that's the best way to do it."
Alex Miller is a writer for Fox News Digital covering the U.S. Senate.

title: Stanford admits breaking own policy after race-, gender-swapped student photos emerge
summary: Stanford University admitted AI was used to alter a dining hall photo, replacing Billy Ramirez with a Black woman amid Trump administration scrutiny.
story: Ashley Webster hosts The Evening Edit Special Edition to question artificial intelligence doomerism. Col. Mike Jernigan (Ret.) and Representative Greg Steube join to discuss political opposition to hyper-regulating AI.
Stanford University was caught red-handed using artificial intelligence to alter an image promoting its residential and dining offerings, replacing a Hispanic male student with a Black woman.
The Stanford Review posted the original dining-hall photo — which shows an Asian woman, a White man and a Hispanic student — alongside the altered version on X.

"We have reviewed the matter and confirmed that AI was used to alter the image in violation of university policy. Stanford's AI policy  is clear: The use of AI in producing or altering images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities, or achievements is strictly prohibited," a spokesperson for Stanford University said in a email to Fox News Digital.

"Both the alteration and lack of disclosure in this case violate that policy. We are working with Residential and Dining Enterprises to provide additional training and ensure proper review of all materials," the spokesperson continued.
KEY TRUMP AGENCY PUTS TOP UNIVERSITIES IN CROSSHAIRS OVER ALLEGED RACE-BASED DORM PROGRAMS

A Stanford Residential and Dining Enterprises promotional image was altered using AI to replace a male student with a Black woman, left, while the original image is shown at right. (The Stanford Review)
Billy Ramirez, who was removed from the photo, told the Stanford Review that he was "baffled" when he saw that he was cut out of the photo.
"At first, I found it hilarious that they had used AI to completely change our appearances, including my race and gender," Ramirez told the Stanford Review.

"But after looking at the comparison, I was also upset because I don’t agree with Stanford making those choices about how we were represented," Ramirez continued. "Seeing my identity changed and being left out of the picture made me feel, in a way, silenced and erased from a representation that was supposed to include me."
"Our reporting highlights the need for universities to abandon not just the practice of DEI but the hyper-fixation on the appearance of diversity," the Stanford Review told Fox News Digital.
In addition to removing Ramirez from the photo, the appearances of the two students were also altered, making the Asian woman and White man’s faces thinner.
FLORIDA STATE UNIVERSITY HIT WITH FEDERAL CIVIL RIGHTS INVESTIGATION OVER RACE, SEX-BASED SCHOLARSHIP PROGRAMS
Stanford University campus in California. (David Butow/Corbis via Getty Images)
The controversy comes as Stanford faces scrutiny from the Trump administration over alleged race-based discrimination in both its admissions policies and a teacher-certification support program.

In April, the Trump administration opened a civil-rights investigation into Stanford over allegations that a teacher-certification program reserved full financial support for educators who identified as people of color. The Education Department said it is examining whether the program violated Title VI by conditioning access to benefits on race.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

And in March 2025, the Justice Department launched an investigation into Stanford along with several other universities over whether it was using diversity, equity and inclusion in admission decisions. The outcome of the Stanford admissions review has not been publicly announced.
Elaine Mallon is a writer for Fox News Digital and Fox Business covering national politics.

title: China ‘throwing gasoline on the fire’ in AI data centers race, say lawmakers
summary: Jason Smith and John Moolenaar allege the Chinese Communist Party is exploiting tax-exempt nonprofits while 'waging an influence campaign' against American AI
story: Rep. Jason Smith told Fox News Digital that pro-China nonprofits are fueling opposition to U.S. data centers as lawmakers urge Treasury and the IRS to investigate their tax-exempt status.

FIRST ON FOX: As President Donald Trump prepares to meet with Chinese leader Xi Jinping about the future of artificial intelligence, two top House Republicans are warning that the Chinese Communist Party is "throwing gasoline on the fire" by undermining America's effort to build out AI infrastructure.

In a new letter disclosed to Fox News Digital, House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Jason Smith, R-Mo., and House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party Chairman John Moolenaar, R-Mich., asked Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and IRS Chief Executive Officer Frank Bisignano to determine whether money has been funneled from overseas through America’s charitable system to block the data centers needed for the U.S. to compete with China.

Specifically, they raised questions about hundreds of millions of dollars that American-born communist tech tycoon Neville Roy Singham pumped into nonprofits and organizations that are now among the leading organizations fighting data center development throughout the country. Recipients of Singham's largesse include the Party for Socialism and Liberation and the ANSWER Coalition, both self-described pro-China communist groups. Earlier this month, activists from both groups carried signs in a Chapel Hill, N.C., protest, merging anti-Trump sentiments with support for communist Cuba and opposition to data centers and AI development, including the message, "SHUT IT DOWN!"

"Under no circumstances can we allow an adversary, and our most serious competitor in AI infrastructure, to weaponize our own tax code and harm an emerging American industry," the lawmakers wrote in the letter, sent on Tuesday.
FROM AUSTIN TO NEW YORK, PRO-CHINA NETWORK FUELS WEEK OF ANTI-US PROTESTS AS XI MEETS TRUMP

Demonstrators protest against AI and data centers as they march on the campus of the University of North Carolina toward the site of the G20 Innovation Ministerial in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, on Sept. 2, 2026. They carry signs branded with the Party for Socialism and Liberation, a pro-China communist group. (Matt Ramey/AFP via Getty Images)

The lawmakers allege that influence operations linked to China are exploiting tax-exempt organizations, nonprofit networks and social media campaigns to fuel opposition to the data centers needed to power America’s AI industry.

The lawmakers urged the agencies to investigate whether tax-exempt organizations connected to the network have operated for the "private or political benefit of foreign-aligned interests" and whether donor-advised funds and intermediary entities were used to "launder the origin of foreign-directed money into American advocacy."

A Fox News Digital investigation found that Singham funneled $285 million since 2017 to six U.S. nonprofits, including his wife Jodie Evan's group, CodePink, through two shell corporations and a donor-advised philanthropy fund run by Goldman Sachs, which said it closed the Singham account in 2024.

The nonprofits have functioned with tax-deductible status while actively involved in promoting communist regimes such as China, coordinating street protests and fomenting anti-American rage. They have denied being part of any foreign influence operation, and Singham hasn't responded to requests for comment.
Smith said China is helping fuel opposition to American artificial intelligence infrastructure by giving a base to Singham as he funds U.S. nonprofit groups involved in anti-data-center protests.
"This is the Chinese helping throw the gasoline on the fire," Smith told Fox News Digital. "The American people need to know that this is not just an organic movement."

Smith said Americans have legitimate concerns about data centers, including their effect on electricity costs and water usage. But he said foreign-backed organizations shouldn't be allowed to exploit those concerns to slow U.S. technological development.
Smith said that "the Chinese want to stall and slow down the advancement of AI in the United States because they want to win the AI war."
"Tax exempt is a privilege. It is not a right," Smith said. "We need to make sure that we’re not subsidizing tax dollars to help create hostility and unrest in our country."

Smith also called for greater transparency regarding the flow of money among organizations connected to Singham. He added that the broader issue extends beyond the tax code and could include questions about compliance with the Foreign Agents Registration Act violations. "Transparency is the biggest thing," he said.
PROBE INTO 'SUBVERSIVE' ANTI-AI SINGHAM NETWORK IS 'ENORMOUS,' FORMER TREASURY ADVISOR SAYS

A Tempe resident wearing a t-shirt from the Party for Socialism and Liberation speaks in opposition of a proposed AI data center in Chandler, Ariz., at a city council meeting on Dec. 11, 2025. (City of Chandler, Arizona)

Moolenaar said organizations presenting themselves as grassroots opposition groups are actually advancing the Chinese Communist Party’s agenda in the U.S. "Groups that portray themselves as grassroots are really more astroturf — very fake — being funded by entities that are working in partnership with the Chinese Communist Party," Moolenaar told Fox News Digital.

"The concern is that they are manipulating the messaging and opposition to different American investments, whether it’s data centers or other technological advances, trying to turn the American people against these technologies so that China would be able to have dominance in this area," he said.
Moolenaar pointed to the use of grassroots organizations, community groups, propaganda and online bots.
"We don’t want foreign entities of concern — countries that may be opposed to American interests — using our system against the American people and trying to manipulate them," Moolenaar said.
He said the lawmakers are seeking greater transparency into the organizations’ funding and tax-exempt status, including whether their political activity violates federal rules.
"When you see them actively speaking out against American interests and realize that groups like CodePink are aggressively funded by this network, that raises serious concerns," Moolenaar said.
The chairman said China’s influence efforts exploit the openness of American society.

"The Chinese Communist Party always has the goal of dividing Americans, manipulating and getting their propaganda out," he said. "They don’t have the freedoms that we enjoy, and they try to exploit our freedoms and use that against us."
China remains both a major trading partner and a strategic competitor, Moolenaar said, but the United States must avoid becoming dependent on Beijing.

"They are a serious adversary," he said. "They are a trading partner, which is true, and we need to have a relationship with them," Moolenaar said. "But at the same time, we do not want to be manipulated, we do not want to become more dependent, and we certainly do not want to be under their thumb."
POWER COUPLE OF CHAOS: HOW A TYCOON AND ACTIVIST BUILT A ‘REVOLUTIONARY BASE’ AT THE HOUSE OF SINGHAM
CodePink co-founder Medea Benjamin holds up a poster from a campaign the nonprofit started, called "China Is Not Our Enemy." (Getty Images)

The lawmakers noted that a bicameral group of congressional committees, including the Ways and Means Committee, the House Select Committee on the CCP and the Senate Intelligence Committee, has been examining how influence operations linked to the CCP allegedly exploit America’s tax-exempt sector to "sow discord and undermine our democracy."

"The CCP consistently identifies political issues under public debate in our country and seeks to corrupt those debates," Smith and Moolenaar wrote in their letter. The CCP, they added, seeks to "heighten divisions between Americans and to degrade our civic processes."
The lawmakers specifically pointed to opposition campaigns targeting the construction of data centers, which are critical to the nation’s AI infrastructure.

A June report from OpenAI identified two clusters of ChatGPT accounts likely originating in China that were used in covert influence operations targeting U.S. debates over AI and technology policy. One campaign, dubbed "Data Center Bandwagon," generated social media comments and images claiming that data-center construction was raising electricity prices for average families. OpenAI said it found no evidence that the operation achieved meaningful breakout beyond its own activity, but said it demonstrated how foreign operators can exploit existing local concerns to amplify distrust.
CHINESE BOT FARM CAUGHT RED-HANDED TRYING TO INFLUENCE HEATED AI DATA CENTER DEBATE

Bitcoin Policy Institute releases a map of protests against data centers by activists from the Party for Socialism and Liberation, a part of the network funded by American Marxist tycoon Neville Roy Singham. (Bitcoin Policy Institute)

The lawmakers also cited a report from the Bitcoin Policy Institute that identified 21 campaigns against data centers led by the Party for Socialism and Liberation across 14 states. The report said those campaigns contributed to 10 data-center moratoria, a permanent data-center ban and four rejected or scrapped projects, representing nearly $23.68 billion in proposed investment.

The Party for Socialism and LIberation and the ANSWER Coalition are supported by the Singham network, and a Fox News Digital investigation has traced links between prominent activism against data centers by the Party for Socialism and Liberation, the ANSWER Coalition and other organizations in the Singham network, including BreakThrough News, the People’s Forum, Tricontinental: Institute for Social Research and CodePink.

"Our tax code should not be used as a shield for foreign money waging a disinformation war on American AI infrastructure," Smith and Moolenaar wrote. "This is yet another shocking and dangerous example of how malign foreign actors are funneling dollars into the United States to further CCP interests."
LAWMAKERS SAY THEY ARE STANDING AT THE GATES AGAINST 'TROJAN HORSES' PROMOTING MALIGN FOREIGN INTERESTS

Demonstrators from the Party for Socialism and Liberation and the ANSWER Coalition protest against AI and data centers as a police officer looks on during the G20 Innovation Ministerial in Chapel Hill, N.C., on Sept. 2, 2026. (Matt Ramey/AFP via Getty Images)
The lawmakers asked Treasury and the IRS to determine whether tax-exempt organizations supporting the network have violated the requirements of their status.

Their request includes examining whether organizations operating under Section 501(c)(3) have acted for the "private or political benefit of foreign-aligned interests," rather than for genuine charitable purposes. They also asked whether donor-advised funds and intermediary entities were used to "launder the origin of foreign-directed money into American advocacy."
The letter follows earlier oversight by the Ways and Means Committee and the House Select Committee on the CCP into the tax-exempt sector and organizations allegedly connected to Singham’s network.

The lawmakers emphasized that opposition to data centers is a legitimate subject for public debate but said Americans should know whether foreign adversaries are attempting to influence those debates through nonprofit organizations, social media campaigns or covert funding channels.

title: Kamala Harris’ Detroit speech sets internet ablaze as critics zero in on noticeable change: ‘It’s so bad’
summary: Kamala Harris faced accusations of using a fake accent at a Detroit NAACP event, fueling speculation about a potential 2028 presidential run.
story: Former Vice President Kamala Harris drew attention at an NCAAP event in Detroit, Michigan for revealing what critics called a new "accent."
Former Vice President Kamala Harris was accused of adopting a different accent during a Detroit NAACP appearance Tuesday, drawing criticism online over the way she addressed the crowd.

Harris made the remarks Tuesday while urging Democratic turnout ahead of the 2026 midterms, but clips of her appearance quickly drew attention online for something else – critics said her delivery sounded noticeably different from her usual speaking voice.

"Shirley Chisholm talked about it. If you're not at the table, bring a folding chair. Otherwise, you might be on the menu. I'm conflating two people say, you know. It's OK to not be in love with a candidate," said Harris. "It's OK to vote and ask everybody else to vote, because this choice is better than that one."
SOCIAL MEDIA ERUPTS AFTER HARRIS INTRODUCES 'MOB BOSS' ACCENT TO ATTACK TRUMP: 'TOTAL CRINGE'
Former Vice President Kamala Harris speaks at the 38th Annual Michigan Democratic Women's Caucus Legacy Luncheon in Detroit, Mich., on April 18, 2026. (Bill Pugliano/Getty Images)
Critics online singled out part of her speech, saying she put on a new "accent."
"Kamala Harris unveiled a new blaccent at an NAACP event in Detroit tonight. This pretty much confirms it. She's running in 2028," posted popular account End Wokeness along with a clip of her speech.
"It’s so bad. Does this mean she’s running," said conservative commentator Benny Johnson.
AOC ACCUSED OF PUTTING ON NEW ACCENT DURING MEMPHIS RALLY: 'GOING FULL KAMALA'
Former Vice President Kamala Harris joins Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed for a roundtable discussion at Birth Detroit on Sept. 22, 2026. (David Guralnick - Pool/Getty Images)
"New accent = another presidential run," wrote another X user.
"Another classic leftist politician trait: switching accents depending on who they're pandering to," posted one person.
DAVID MARCUS: MAMDANI'S FAUX AFRICAN ACCENT AS TELLING AS IT IS BIZARRE

Former Vice President Kamala Harris speaks during a panel discussion at the Austrian World Summit of the Schwarzenegger Climate Initiative on June 16, 2026, in Vienna, Austria. (Joe Klamar/AFP via Getty Images)
"Please let her talk more… the more she talks the better chance of flipping red," posted one person.
WATCH: KAMALA HARRIS TORCHED OVER ‘ZERO SENSE’ WNBA PEP TALK IN LATEST ‘WORD SALAD’ MOMENT
"Queen Word Salad is drunk again," claimed another user.
"ItS tOtAlLy OrGaNiC," posted one person.

Harris has faced similar criticism before. During the 2024 campaign, critics accused her of adopting a Southern accent at a rally in Atlanta and later pointed to differences in her delivery during Labor Day appearances in Detroit and Pittsburgh.
Harris continues to face questions about whether she will make another run for the White House in 2028. She has kept the door open to a possible campaign but has not said whether she plans to run.
"I have not decided if I’m going to run again," Harris said at the NCAAP event.
