The last national outage happened just last month, and Friday's marks the seventh this year.
Brie Stimson is a Los Angeles-based entertainment and breaking news writer for Fox News Digital.

title: Third person dies after mosquito is reportedly trapped on plane to Germany in 'airport malaria' phenomenon
summary: Three people have died from so-called "airport malaria" after an infected mosquito was reportedly transported aboard a flight to Frankfurt Airport in Germany.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
Three people have died from malaria after a mosquito was transported aboard a flight to Germany, according to reports.
Several people were rushed to a hospital amid a rare outbreak of the tropical disease following flights to Frankfurt, The Sun reported.
It was unclear where the flights departed from.
The third person, a resident of Schwanheim, just north of the airport, died recently. In August, an airport worker also died from the disease. Neither had traveled to a malaria-endemic region.
MEASLES-INFECTED TRAVELER MAY HAVE EXPOSED PASSENGERS AT LAX AND NEARBY HOTEL, HEALTH OFFICIALS WARN

A Lufthansa Airbus A320 sits at Remote Stand V143 at Frankfurt Airport in Kelsterbach, Frankfurt am Main, Hesse. Frankfurt Airport is Germany's main international airport by passenger numbers and is operated by Fraport as the main hub for Lufthansa. (Getty Images)
Another German resident also came down with malaria, which can only be contracted from the bite of an infected mosquito and cannot be spread from human to human.

"Both individuals had become infected with the ​malaria-causing parasite Plasmodium falciparum, even though they had not traveled to a malaria-endemic region and had not worked ​at the airport," city officials said.
DEADLY MOSQUITO-BORNE VIRUS CLAIMS FIRST LIFE IN MAJOR US CITY AS CASES SPREAD
The terrifying phenomenon, known as "airport malaria," occurs when an infected mosquito becomes trapped aboard a plane or inside luggage, is carried to a malaria-free area and bites someone locally.
Three people have died after a mosquito became trapped on a plane to Frankfurt, Germany, officials there said. (iStock)
In July, airport officials set traps around the property to contain the malaria outbreak, The Sun reported.
WEST NILE VIRUS DETECTED IN SOUTHERN STATE AS HEALTH OFFICIALS WARN RESIDENTS ABOUT MOSQUITOES
Germany's Robert Koch Institute, the agency responsible for disease control and public health, said airport workers became ill after contracting malaria between July 4 and July 6.
In total, six employees contracted the disease, according to Fraport, the firm that operates Frankfurt Airport, The Express reported.
Airport workers became sick with malaria between July 4 and July 6. (iStock)

"We have provided comprehensive information to all employees and encourage them to consult a doctor if they experience any symptoms," the firm said.
Louis Casiano is a reporter for Fox News Digital. Story tips can be sent to louis.casiano@fox.com.

title: China firm gave Iran lifeline to collect Hormuz tolls before pulling plug amid US warning
summary: After briefly issuing a web security certificate for a portal linked to Iran's U.S.-sanctioned Persian Gulf Strait Authority, a Shanghai-based firm revoked it, though the move could still draw scrutiny under U.S. sanctions rules
story: Lawyer and former OFAC official Jeremy Paner says even limited services to sanctioned Iranian entities could trigger sanction action.

Iran’s sanctioned Persian Gulf Straits Authority (PGSA) regained secure online access for four days after a Shanghai-based internet security firm provided and then revoked its web credentials, enabling Tehran to vet vessels, collect Strait of Hormuz tolls and operate despite U.S. digital restrictions, global internet monitors said.

TrustAsia issued an automated domain-validated certificate, a routine process that verifies control of a website domain through server checks and typically does not involve manual vetting or background checks.

The move prompted U.S. sanctions experts, including Jeremy Paner, a partner at Hughes Hubbard & Reed, to urge TrustAsia to review its compliance program before offering further services to the IRGC-linked maritime authority — with Paner warning them to act "before it is too late."
The PGSA first said its website was disrupted Aug. 10 because of "the enemy's political influence on the internet service provision systems," according to a post on X.
IRAN REQUESTS TALKS WITH US AS WHITE HOUSE WARNS 'VIOLENCE WILL BE MET WITH VIOLENCE'
Oil tankers and cargo ships line up in the Strait of Hormuz as seen from Mina Al Fajer, United Arab Emirates, Wednesday, March 11, 2026. (Altaf Qadri/AP Photo)

NetBlocks CEO Alp Toker told Fox News Digital that the authority had lost its web security credentials after the entity was added to the U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctions list on May 27.

The loss of standard SSL/TLS certificates, Toker said, made the PGSA website inaccessible using standard browsers. This forced shipping firms to use unencrypted connections that, according to Toker, could leave their data vulnerable to interception.

While no data breaches resulting from the use of these connections have been made known, and there are no known instances in which a shipping firm’s data was intercepted and used to its detriment because of the certificate expiration, Toker said the site’s inaccessibility resulted in a shift to what he described as "insecure protocols."
"The digital transparency records are authoritative on this," he said, adding that the measure forced the traffic into a format that could be readily intercepted.
"This is a class of vulnerability open to government exploitation, rather than a corporate breach or personal data leak."
Toker claimed this could make it easier for authorities to read communications sent through the platform, potentially identifying shipping firms collaborating with the PGSA.
TRUMP SAYS IRAN WILL PAY — WHAT IT TAKES TO END THE WAR REMAINS UNCLEAR

Naval units from Iran and Russia simulate the rescue of a hijacked vessel during joint drills at the Port of Bandar Abbas in Hormozgan, Iran, on Feb. 19, 2026. (Iranian Army/Handout/Anadolu via Getty Images)

"The net result was that the website was more difficult to access, because most web browsers strongly encourage the use of secure HTTPS," Toker said, adding that any form submissions could have been easily "eavesdropped on because they're no longer encrypted in transit."

"The mentioned issue has been resolved, and the secure domain https://pgsa.ir is now once again available for submitting requests using any browser," the PGSA said six days later on Aug. 17 and in another post shared on X.
"If the issue recurs in the future, the HTTP domain will again be temporarily available using the Firefox browser."

Toker confirmed that Iran had turned to Shanghai-based certificate authority TrustAsia Technologies, which he said issued new digital security credentials to the PGSA despite the U.S. sanctions, restoring secure access to its website.

"Iran’s IRGC extorts vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz through the so-called Persian Gulf Strait Authority," the Treasury Department said in May when designating the entity, adding that the PGSA "spearheads an Iranian-controlled scheme that flagrantly violates international law and U.S. sanctions."

"Anyone cooperating with the so-called strait authority may be providing support to and receiving services from the IRGC, which ultimately benefits from this attempted extortion, and may therefore be exposed to sanctions risk," the Treasury Department warned.
The Chinese firm bills itself as a "leading and professionally certified certification authority in China with its focus on trusted, secure and cryptographic communications in the digital world."
Its mission, it says, is to "Build trust everywhere in the digital world."
"Almost all of these root authorities do business with the U.S., so they tend to comply with U.S. sanctions," Toker said.
But TrustAsia, he noted, had "gone its own way, building a China-first certificate infrastructure that sidesteps the West."
Toker said TrustAsia had "simply gone ahead and issued Iran's PGSA with a new certificate, and Iran was once again collecting revenue from ships passing the Strait via its secure online portal."
TRUMP CALLS ON ARAB NATIONS TO SIGN ABRAHAM ACCORDS

The Treasury Building is viewed in Washington, May 4, 2021. The U.S. on Wednesday imposed a new round of sanctions on a group of 20 people and firms allegedly involved in a financial facilitation network for the benefit of the Iranian military. The Treasury Department sanctions impact firms and people spanning from Hong Kong to the United Arab Emirates. (AP Photo/Patrick Semansky)
Paner warned that U.S. authorities would have enforcement powers over such actions.
"The U.S. has incredibly broad authority to impose sanctions on non-Iranian companies that provide any sorts of services to sanctioned Iranian companies," he told Fox News Digital.

"Many times, that authority will be abbreviated or explained as being providers of material support to sanctioned Iranian companies. But in fact, any level of services whatsoever could be the basis for the United States imposing sanctions against the company for providing services to Iran."
"Restoration of the certificate is unequivocally sanctionable," Paner warned.
"Restoring the certificate is/was a service provided to the PGSA, which can be the basis for imposing sanctions pursuant to Executive Order 13224, as amended.

"That authority does not in any way require that the service be ‘knowingly’ provided to the PGSA. In other words, the automated nature of the service is irrelevant and does not make the service any less sanctionable," the lawyer added.
In a statement to Fox News Digital on Aug. 20, a spokesperson for TrustAsia confirmed that the firm issued a "Domain Validated TLS certificate for pgsa.ir."
"Thank you for bringing this matter to our attention," the firm said before clarifying that "DV certificates are issued through automated validation of control over the requested domain names."
IRAN ACCELERATES EXECUTION CAMPAIGN AGAINST ANTI-REGIME ACTIVISTS AMID INTERNET CENSORSHIP
Iranian Navy soldiers on an armed speed boat in the Persian Gulf near the Strait of Hormuz. (Morteza Nikoubazl/NurPhoto via Getty Images)
"This process does not verify or assert the legal identity, affiliation, or sanctions status of the entity operating or benefiting from the domain.

"As a result, the relationship described in your inquiry was not identified during the automated issuance process." Following the firm's review, TrustAsia said it "added the entire pgsa.ir domain namespace to our restricted-issuance list to prevent further issuance or renewal."
"We also expect to complete revocation of the existing certificate within this week," the spokesman said on Aug. 20.
These actions are precautionary compliance and risk-control measures. They should not be interpreted as a finding that the certificate was technically misissued, TrustAsia said.
Toker confirmed the TrustAsia certificate's privilege had been withdrawn on Aug. 21 at 12:15:25 UTC. "This usually means the issuer has taken action," he said.

The internet expert clarified that the revocation will gradually be coming into effect, with the firm "signaling that the PGSA certificate should no longer be trusted, and they're distributing this notice that privilege is withdrawn, usually meaning customer misuse or breached terms of use."
"The secure website will stop working in most browsers, unless the owners can find a certificate authority that's willing to issue a new certificate," Toker said.
IRAN’S UNSEEN SUPREME LEADER BECOMES WEAPON IN ESCALATING POWER STRUGGLE, EXPERTS SAY

Iran sanctions prompt capital flight as Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent reports Iranian leaders allegedly wired tens of millions overseas amid protest crackdowns. (Anna Moneymaker/Saeid Zareian/Picture Alliance via Getty Images)
After reviewing TrustAsia's statement, Paner also said that OFAC would expect the company to "use the discovery as an opportunity to enhance its compliance program before it is too late."
The former OFAC official clarified that Iran's revenue collection in the waterway would likely draw high-level scrutiny in Washington.
"Iran's attempt to extort the world in the movement of oil through the Strait of Hormuz is of the utmost importance to OFAC, which is the agency that implements and enforces U.S. economic sanctions."
Because major U.S. web browsers currently recognize TrustAsia’s root certificates, American systems would have automatically trusted the sanctioned Iranian portal.

Toker claimed the Treasury Department could have found TrustAsia in violation of sanctions for providing material assistance to a blocked entity, potentially forcing tech giants such as Google and Microsoft to revoke trust in TrustAsia.
There is no evidence that this process had begun or was likely to occur.
"This could have splintered the global chain of trust and potentially render much of the Chinese web inaccessible from the West," Toker warned.
IRAN IS NOT A NORMAL NATION YOU CAN MAKE DEALS WITH; IT’S A NATIONAL SECURITY THREAT

Ahmad Vahidi, commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Quds Force, Esmail Qaani, and Iraj Masjedi, deputy coordinator of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Quds Force, participate in a ceremony to mark the memory of former IRGC commander, Hossein Salami, who is killed in Israeli attacks, at a mosque in an IRGC organizational house complex in Tehran, Iran, July 25, 2025. (Morteza Nikoubazl/Nur Photo via Getty Images)
Paner clarified that the certificates authenticate the site, boosting its credibility, and suggested TrustAsia should have weighed the risks of working with sanctioned entities.
"There's always reputational risk involved in any company that decides to do business with the IRGC."
"If I were advising TrustAsia, I would at minimum immediately identify all other IRGC companies receiving services."
Paner added that this latest situation aligned with broader warnings from administration officials.

"I think this dovetails pretty nicely with Secretary Bessent's comments about how the coming sanctions are going to be unlike any that has come prior. Sanctions require a careful balancing of the costs and the benefits.
"When it's a Chinese tech company providing necessary services to the IRGC, I'm confident that the U.S. government is going to forego any sort of balancing in that regard."

The United States on Aug. 24 had sanctioned nearly 60 Iran-linked individuals, entities and vessels and expanded the threat of secondary sanctions, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said. These did not include TrustAsia.

Bessent described the measures as part of an "economic onslaught" targeting Tehran’s global financial networks under "Operation Economic Outcast."
A Chinese Embassy spokesperson also said in a statement: "I am not aware of the specifics you mentioned. I have no information to provide."
Fox News Digital reached out to the U.S. Department of the Treasury and the White House for comment.

Emma Bussey is a breaking news writer for Fox News Digital. Before joining Fox, she worked at The Telegraph with the U.S. overnight team, across desks including foreign, politics, news, sport and culture.

title: ‘Voters get to choose — just not the result’: Russia’s parliamentary election reaches occupied Ukraine
summary: Russian State Duma elections will be held in occupied Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson, and Zaporizhzhia amid accusations of armed voter intimidation.
story: FDD's Keti Korkiya says Russians are likely scared to give pollsters their real opinions on Putin and the war ahead of Friday's election.

Russian State Duma elections began Friday — the first since the invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Voting is also taking place in the areas annexed from Ukraine in the east as Putin looks to reinforce popular support for the war.
OSCE election observers are not invited to monitor the outcome of the elections, a telling signal, critics say, that the Kremlin has no intentions of conducting free and fair elections.

"Russia’s refusal to invite an election observation mission seriously breaches its international commitments and shows a worrying disregard for democratic standards. Election observation is not optional — it is something that all OSCE participating States have agreed to, and it is a cornerstone of transparency and accountability," OSCE Parliamentary Assembly President Pere Joan Pons told Fox News Digital.
Russian President Vladimir Putin holds a Security Council meeting in Moscow on Friday, Aug. 7, 2026. (Alexander Kazakov/Pool Sputnik Kremlin via AP)
Russia enacted strict censorship laws after the invasion, criminalizing any dissent about the operation or the armed forces and spreading misinformation about the war.
CIA DIRECTOR JOHN RATCLIFFE MET WITH RUSSIAN INTELLIGENCE OFFICIALS IN VISIT TO MOSCOW, KREMLIN SAYS

As the Kremlin has tried to keep popular support in favor of its war against Ukraine, a Russian court sentenced Lev Shlosberg, a vocal critic and leader of one of Russia’s only opposition parties to over 11 years in a penal colony for criticizing the war. Prior to Shlosberg’s sentencing, Russia's Supreme Court banned his opposition Yabloko Party from participating in September’s Duma elections.
There are nine parties on the list, all supportive of Putin, including the Kremlin's own United Party in the elections, The Associated Press reported.

Shortly after Russia’s invasion in 2022, Moscow unilaterally annexed portions of occupied Ukrainian territory in Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson and Zaporizhzhia. In 2023, Russian President Vladimir Putin signed legislation allowing elections to take place in the occupied territories. Ukraine and the international community do not recognize Russian sovereignty over the occupied regions.

Elections in Russia, and by extension in the occupied territory, are seen by his critics as window-dressing opportunities used by Putin to highlight his narrative that the war in Ukraine and the annexation of Ukrainian territory was a legitimate and lawful action.

Keti Korkiya from the Foundation for Defense of Democracies Russia Program told Fox News Digital that, "Russians are ready to support, symbolically, Putin, the Kremlin and the war, but if they have to pay a personal price, or even [an] economic price, they are unwilling to do that. That's why Russia has not done another wave of mobilization."
Firefighters put out the fire in a multi-story apartment building following a Russian missile attack in Kharkiv, Ukraine, on Saturday, March 7, 2026. (Andrii Marienko/AP)
The upcoming elections, like most elections in Russia, will take place under a climate of pervasive fear and manipulation, not the freedom to exercise a democratic right, according to critics.
"It’s a total regime of terror," Jaroslava Barbieri, research fellow at the Ukraine Forum at Chatham House, told Fox News Digital.

The last time Russian elections were held in the occupied territories was in 2024, when Putin secured a fifth term in office, winning nearly 90% of the vote. Residents in occupied Ukraine were forced to acquire Russian passports, which is how authorities are able to compile lists of voters.
FORMER GEORGIAN PRIME MINISTER SAYS NATION'S ELECTION WAS 'RIGGED,' AND 'WRITTEN IN MOSCOW'
A woman casts her ballot at a mobile polling station during early voting in Russia's presidential election in Donetsk, Russian-occupied Ukraine, on March 14, 2024. (Stringer/AFP via Getty Images)

"Election officials are escorted by Russian soldiers carrying ballot boxes door-to-door. Ostensibly framed as a security measure against Ukrainian partisan strikes, this is about direct intimidation, and it is a flagrant violation of international law," Barbieri added.

President Vladimir Putin said in August that the State Duma elections will reaffirm Russia's stability on the world stage, noting the election will highlight the "maturity" of Russia’s political system and resilience in the face of foreign aggression, according to Turkey's Anadolu Agency.

Russia’s Central Election Commission (CEC) approved new electoral regulations that will be implemented in occupied Ukraine. The Commission stressed the importance of early and at-home voting to prevent large gatherings which could be exploited by Ukrainian attacks.

Russia's ministry of foreign affairs posted on X that preparations for overseas voting in Russia’s State Duma elections are nearly complete. It said there are 326 polling stations set up at Russian embassies and consulates in 152 countries.
Volodymyr Ariev, a member of the Ukrainian Parliament, said people living in temporarily occupied Ukrainian territories should boycott the staged Russian elections.

"Any sort of elections held in the temporarily occupied Ukrainian territories is illegal and a breach of international law. Ukraine will never recognize any person ‘elected’ as a member of Parliament in the temporarily occupied territories," Ariev told Fox News Digital.
Ariev said people living in the occupied east should leave their homes and spend election day someplace else, to avoid being coerced into voting.
PUTIN PLANS FOR NEXT 6-YEAR TERM AS RUSSIANS VOTE IN 'NEITHER FREE NOR FAIR ELECTION'

Ivana Stradner, who focuses on Russian information security and influence operations at the FDD, says as Russia’s battlefield momentum stalls, the costs of war mount, and Ukraine brings the conflict to Russia’s doorstep, Putin is seeking political legitimacy this election.

"The State Duma elections give the Kremlin a chance to manufacture the appearance of public support… not only for United Russia, but for continuing Putin’s aggression in Ukraine. When the battlefield gets harder to sell, the ballot box becomes another way to sell the war," Stradner told Fox News Digital.
A soldier fires a third-generation Javelin man-portable anti-tank missile system during a professional training session on Jan. 7, 2026, in Ukraine. (Ukrinform/NurPhoto via Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

In the 2024 presidential elections, the annexed Donetsk People’s Republic and Luhansk People’s Republic delivered well above the current targeted 70% support, voting well over 90% for President Putin.
"Apparently, in Putin’s version of democracy, the voters get to choose… just not the result," Stradner added. The three days of voting ends on September 20.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: U.S. and China agree to extend trade truce through Jan. 10, Bessent says
summary: The agreement extends the suspension of some tariffs as Chinese President Xi Jinping arrives in Washington for a state visit.
story: The United States and China have agreed to extend a bilateral trade truce that was set to expire in November through Jan. 10, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Wednesday.
The announcement came after Bessent and China’s vice premier, He Lifeng, held an unscheduled meeting in Washington.

“We will extend what we call the ‘Busan Agreement’ — the economic détente between the two countries that was scheduled to end on Nov. 10 — that is going to be extended until Jan. 10,” Bessent said in an interview on Fox News Channel.
Bessent said it’s possible a larger economic package will be agreed upon by January. But it’s also possible to “just roll the current deal” and extend it further.
Trump welcomes Xi at Joint Base Andrews

“There are some deliverables that have not been perfect on the Chinese side, so we also want to see, now that we’ve sat down and told them our expectations, if over the coming months they can be more fulsome in enacting the agreement,” he said.
The announcement, a big win for economic stability in both countries, came only minutes after Chinese President Xi Jinping touched down to begin a multiday state visit to Washington.

Bessent also indicated that there could be further announcements in coming days from the Chinese delegation, including agreements to buy more American agricultural products and potential deals in the financial services sector.
Since Sunday, Bessent and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer have been holding talks with their Chinese counterparts to lay the groundwork for the closely watched state visit.
On Sunday, Bessent and Greer announced that the U.S. and China had proposed exchanging alerts about AI-related hacking incidents, especially those that concern national security.
The U.S. and China could also agree on lists of goods on which lower tariffs would be applied as part of President Donald Trump’s “Board of Trade” initiative with China, Greer told reporters.

“We expect that the types of goods you’ll see in those lists are consumer goods, low-tech items coming in from the Chinese side,” he said. “On the U.S. side, energy products, agricultural goods, potentially medical devices and other things like that.”
Xi’s trip is his first state visit to the U.S. in more than a decade.

News of the trade truce extension is likely to be widely welcomed in Washington and Beijing, given that the U.S. and China are vital sources of goods for each other and for their millions of consumers and businesses.

title: These young quarterbacks were supposed to break out. Now they’re hurt.
summary: The New York Giants’ Jaxson Dart on Monday became the latest upstart QB to be sidelined with an injury, joining the Bears’ Caleb Williams and the Commanders’ Jayden Daniels as signal callers who had to leave the field early in Week 2.
story: The New York Giants were one of the NFL’s pleasant surprises in Week 1, beginning the John Harbaugh era with an impressive win over the Dallas Cowboys thanks in large part to the play of second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart.

The Giants’ dreams of a turnaround season quickly hit a roadblock on Monday, however, as Dart became the latest upstart QB to be sidelined with an injury. And now Dart may miss the rest of the regular season after imaging on Tuesday revealed his knee was hurt worse than the team initially feared, according to multiple reports.
Only two weeks into the NFL season, several of the game’s young stars are seeing their seasons upended due to varying degrees of injuries.

Dart joined the Chicago Bears’ Caleb Williams and the Washington Commanders’ Jayden Daniels as signal callers who had to leave the field early in Week 2. That trio joined a list of sidelined quarterbacks that also includes the Minnesota Vikings’ Kyler Murray and the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks’ Sam Darnold.
All five of those players are former first-round draft picks — and all are under the age of 30.

Dart left in the first quarter of New York’s 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. On a third-and-8 pass attempt, Dart was sandwiched by multiple players as the pocket collapsed around him, and he took a substantial hit to his left knee from a Rams linebacker.
Dart limped off the field and was taken back to the locker room. After initially being ruled questionable to return, he was ruled out for good in the second half.
“He’s going to be OK,” Giants general manager Joe Schoen told ESPN’s Laura Rutledge during the “Monday Night Football” broadcast, adding that Dart would undergo X-rays at the stadium.
Dart’s hard-charging play style raised eyebrows during his rookie season, when he missed time due to a concussion but seemingly refused to tone down his aggressiveness when he returned.
During the preseason, Dart even expressed confusion at why he so often is required to enter the blue medical tent on the sidelines.

“I really respect the rules, and the thought behind, you know, the NFL has of keeping players healthy and reviewing things,” Dart said in August after a big hit required he undergo a mandatory medical evaluation. “But at the same time, I’m still puzzled by just feeling like every time that I get hit, you know, I just find my way in there.”
Dart’s injury Monday, though, came on a relatively routine pass play, highlighting how no quarterback is ever truly safe.

The same can be said of the Commanders’ Daniels, who dislocated his left elbow while trying to regain his balance after he was tripped by one of his own lineman in a 37-20 loss to the Cowboys. Daniels, the 2024 Offensive Rookie of the Year, dislocated the same elbow last season, in which he appeared in only seven games due to multiple injuries.
“It sucks for him,” Washington coach Dan Quinn told reporters Monday. “I know how much these guys put into it. So, when there are setbacks like this, you just want to stand by them.”

A little before Daniels’ exit, the Bears’ Williams was carted off the field with a hamstring strain in a 9-3 loss to the Vikings. While Williams’ emotional exit from the game quickly became a social media meme, it also cut short what had been an exciting start to the season. Chicago was coming off a Week 1 in which it had scored 59 points.
“He’s right now working through every avenue that he’s got available to get back on track here. We’ll see what that looks like,” Bears coach Ben Johnson told reporters Monday.
Johnson added that Williams has an ability to recover quickly, and his injury is considered week-to-week.
While the Bears, Giants and the Commanders all lost after their starters went down, their seasons are far from over.
The Vikings lost Murray in Week 1 but still managed a 2-0 start to the season with Carson Wentz at the helm. And now Murray is expected to start in Week 3 after recovering from a concussion.

The Seahawks are also 2-0 with Drew Lock playing in place of Darnold, and even exploded for 31 points on Sunday. Darnold is expected to return to practice this week, though his starting status is up in the air.
For now, the Bears will turn to Tyler Bagent, the Giants to Jameis Winston, and the Commanders to Marcus Mariota as the three clubs try to keep their seasons afloat without their young leaders.

And Dart, Williams and Daniels — all three of whom have flashed potential to not only be great players but stewards for the league because of their exciting style of play — will have to wait a little longer to cement their star turns.

title: 8 Navy members attempted suicide on the USS Lincoln during extended deployment, military official says
summary: The ship, which supported the U.S. war with Iran, was at sea for nearly 300 days without a port call.
story: Eight Navy members aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln have attempted suicide since the beginning of their extended deployment, a top Navy official said in a letter obtained by NBC News.

The length of the deployment, which some service members on board the carrier had described as extraordinarily tough, has raised concerns about supply shortages and the effect on sailors’ mental health.
No deaths have been attributed to suicide during the deployment.

The number of suicide attempts includes those by crewmembers and sailors from the carrier air wing, strike group and destroyer squadron staff; escorting destroyers; and all embarked aviation squadrons, according to the letter, which acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao sent to Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand, D-N.Y.
About 7,500 service members, primarily sailors, are part of the strike group.
A Navy official said the letter was delivered to Gillibrand on Tuesday.

The official said the number of sailors who jumped overboard while the Lincoln was in the Middle East providing operations for the war in Iran remains at two, as previously reported. The official did not provide details about the six other attempts.
In the letter, Cao answered a series of questions that Gillibrand, a member of the Armed Services Committee, had asked Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in a previous letter.
The letter also addressed Gillibrand’s concerns about conditions and medical resources aboard the Lincoln.
In a statement, Gillibrand said the conditions on the ship were “serious and deteriorating.”
“Our troops and their families make immense sacrifices every single day, yet the president dismissed them with open disrespect,” she said.
President Donald Trump has previously said the deployment was “not nearly long enough.”
The ship was at sea without a port call for 286 days supporting the U.S. war with Iran. A typical deployment is six to seven months, with regular stops to replenish food supplies.

The Lincoln left San Diego in November. Its deployment was supposed to end in May, but it was extended after the war began in February. The ship stopped in Thailand this month and is now sailing back to San Diego after a stop in Guam.

Relatives of those on board raised concerns about food shortages and low morale and how the extended time at sea was “wreaking havoc” on sailors’ mental health, as one relative described it to NBC News last month.

Some military officials have played down or rejected those claims. In an op-ed in The Wall Street Journal last month, Adm. Brad Cooper, the commander of U.S. Central Command, described the concerns as “old news” that were resolved months ago.
This summer, a Navy official said that officials had not observed an increase in suicidal ideations or attempts aboard the ship and that service members’ well-being was a top priority.

“We take every service member’s well-being seriously and have religious, medical and mental health professionals available to assess and address concerns as they arise,” the official said in a statement.

The Lincoln has five chaplains, a clinical psychologist, a clinical social worker, behavioral health technicians and an embedded integrated prevention coordination counselor to support the crew, the Navy official said.

If you or someone you know is struggling or in emotional distress, call or text 988 or chat at 988lifeline.org 24/7 to reach the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. For additional resources, visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources.

title: Sunny Hostin reveals she was holdout juror in 1991 ‘Butcher of Tompkins Square Park’ trial
summary: Hostin said on “The View” that she changed her fellow jurors’ minds to find Daniel Rakowitz not criminally responsible by reason of insanity at his 1991 New York City trial.
story: “The View” host Sunny Hostin revealed that she was the holdout juror in the high-profile “Butcher of Tompkins Square Park” trial in 1991.
Hostin spoke about her time serving on that jury during a discussion about the Lindsay Clancy case, which ended this month in a mistrial with the jury split 11-1.

“The reason I felt that I feel so strongly about this holdout juror is because I was a holdout juror in a case, in the Daniel Rakowitz case,” Hostin said on Tuesday’s episode, to the shock of her castmates.

Rakowitz was accused of killing and dismembering Monika Beerle, a 26-year-old dance student, then boiling her body parts and feeding them in a soup to people in Tompkins Square Park in the East Village of Manhattan in 1989.
He was found not guilty by reason of insanity at his 1991 trial, which dominated headlines.
Hostin said she served on the jury before she went to law school.
“When I brought it up at the Hot Topics meeting, I don’t think everyone believed me. And then my producer looked it up, and I’m in The New York Times,” she said.

The show then aired a picture of a newspaper clipping from an old New York Times article that read: “Several jurors questioned afterward said one holdout juror was principally responsible for preventing them from returning a guilty verdict.”

“That was me,” Hostin said. “It was because I saw clearly that he was psychotic. He was in psychosis. He did not mean to kill her, and once he killed her, he panicked. He chopped up her body parts. Yes, boiled her body parts. Tried to commit the perfect crime ... and he fed her body parts to the unhoused.”
The jury deliberated for an intense nine days, and its talks were at times combative, Hostin recalled.

“One juror threw a chair at me they were so angry with me. But one by one I picked them off and said: ‘What about this? What about that?’ And we ended up all 12 unanimously voting that he was not criminally responsible by reason of insanity,” she said.
Rakowitz was ordered in 2010 to remain at maximum-security Kirby Forensic Psychiatric Center on Ward’s Island.
Hostin noted that Rakowitz remains in a mental institution, which she called “a different type of prison.”
Her castmates were stunned by Hostin’s revelation, some appearing to disagree with her position in the jury.
Co-host Alyssa Farah Griffin said, “And you got this guy off?” as Hostin described the grisly crime. Star Jones, who was seated next to Hostin, joked, “Excuse me, can I move over?”
Speaking about the Clancy case, Hostin called Massachusetts’ insanity defense “well-established” and said she agreed Clancy was not criminally responsible by reason of insanity.
Clancy’s defense argued she was not criminally responsible for killing her three children because she was suffering from postpartum psychosis.

Some jurors have said one holdout juror did not want to acquit. That juror, Michael P. Desronvil, spoke out last week, saying in a statement, “Based on all the physical evidence, key witnesses, and what the prosecution presented, I thought it was enough proof that she [Clancy] knew exactly what she was doing and planned.”

title: Bernie Sanders and Greg Casar propose AI ‘superintelligence’ ban with a 20-year jail penalty
summary: New legislation authored by Sen. Sanders, I-Vt., and Rep. Casar, D-Texas, also calls for a Cabinet-level secretary of AI to regulate artificial intelligence.
story: WASHINGTON — Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., and Rep. Greg Casar, D-Texas, rolled out an aggressive bill Wednesday to rein in artificial intelligence, escalating the debate on Capitol Hill.

The 19-page Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act would require pausing advanced AI development until a Cabinet-level Department of Artificial Intelligence, led by a secretary of AI, can be created to regulate and supervise it.
Violating the rules would come with what they called the “corporate death penalty” plus up to 20 years in jail, which Sanders said is the same penalty as unlawfully building nuclear weapons.

The bill is one of the most aggressive of a series of congressional proposals to regulate AI. While AI was a major topic of discussion on Capitol Hill as researchers warned of cataclysmic possibilities this month, there’s little expectation that any meaningful legislation will pass this year.
In Congress, “virtually nothing is happening to prepare us for the tsunami that is coming,” Sanders told reporters on a call Wednesday.
Add to Google
Add to Google

His bill with Casar includes a list of precursors that seek to define the development of “superintelligence,” including: “The capacity to automate or greatly accelerate the process of artificial intelligence research and development.”

The goal is to bar recursive self-improvement, according to an aide involved in developing the bill. Some AI specialists have warned that recursive self-improvement could lead to AI systems’ training themselves to get smarter and more capable, eventually escaping human control.

“We’re dealing with something that humanity has never seen before. It is clearly the most transformational technology in the history of the world, and it is moving very, very rapidly,” Sanders said on Wednesday’s call. “When we deal with AI, it has been developed and it is being pushed by a handful, a small number, of the wealthiest people on Earth. And their main goal is to simply increase their wealth and power.”

Experts say defining “superintelligence” at a technical level will prove messy given fuzzy boundaries among different levels of AI capabilities. The lines were further blurred by President Donald Trump’s announcement that he would rename “artificial intelligence” to “super intelligence” for the purposes of government documents in his speech Tuesday at the United Nations General Assembly.

The Sanders-Casar bill drew praise from the leaders of ControlAI, an advocacy group pushing for guardrails on the technology. They wrote in a blog post: “We appreciate the choice to define superintelligent AI by its capability to overpower the federal government. This targets exactly the kind of AI development that poses a risk of extinction, without having to settle in advance the technical details of how such an AI would work.”

Kevin Frazier, an AI policy expert and professor at the University of Texas School of Law, also commended the lawmakers’ efforts. “The ban proposed by Sen. Sanders and Rep. Casar rightfully acknowledges that Congress needs to act quickly to ensure that AI development does not lead to unintended and irreversible negative consequences,” he told NBC News.

However, Frazier said the bill ignores other avenues to prevent AI-fueled harms. He highlighted existing proposals to establish independent verification organizations that could help shed light on leading AI companies’ safety practices — a proposal that has gained momentum in the past week in Silicon Valley and at the U.N. General Assembly.
Others in Washington argued that Sanders and Casar’s effort is provocative but unrealistic.

“Sen. Sanders’ bill will be dead on arrival with both the AI industry and Washington,” according to Caleb Max, president and CEO of the National AI Association, a Washington-based trade group that advocates for business-friendly AI legislation.
“Some CEOs would say we have already crossed the threshold set out in the bill, meaning this is a de facto AI ban,” Max said.
He also said the penalties outlined in the bill are “likely unconstitutional and, again, poorly defined.”
Other lawmakers are proposing bills that address concerns about advanced cybersecurity capabilities that have already materialized.

Sen. Maria Cantwell, D-Wash., the ranking member of the Commerce Committee, said she is working on a bill to establish meaningful guardrails on advanced AI systems and outlined a series of principles that should be part of any federal AI rules.

“The federal government has to be involved in standard-setting. I don’t care whether you’re a chemical company, a nuclear company or an AI company. The federal government needs to set standards,” Cantwell told NBC News.
“You have to have independent testing,” she said.

“You need to work on an international strategy,” she added, arguing that the president “should be talking to the Chinese about — what are you going to do to, basically, alert each other on escapes of AI agent swarming practices and have a red phone to talk about it. ... You need to have an incident reporting system with international partners.”

Trump is scheduled to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington, D.C., beginning Wednesday evening. AI is likely to be a topic of discussion, with OpenAI’s Sam Altman, Apple’s Tim Cook, Trump’s former AI czar, David Sacks, and others attending a state dinner for Xi on Thursday night.

After a meeting with a Chinese delegation Sunday, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said he had proposed creating a notification mechanism to alert the other country about severe AI incidents. It is unclear whether that mechanism will be implemented.
If Democrats win control of the Senate in the Nov. 3 midterm elections, Cantwell is in line to chair the Commerce Committee.

The current chair is Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, who is working on a separate bill with Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., and Sen. Amy Klobuchar, D-Minn. Cruz has said it will “address the catastrophic risks,” including biological or nuclear threats.
“We’re continuing to work and negotiate to reach bipartisan agreements,” Cruz told NBC News on Monday, without giving a timeline to release text of the bill. “We’re not there yet.”

AI safety advocates have criticized the Cruz-Thune-Klobuchar proposal for being too light-touch. The groups say any AI regulation must mandate safety testing, while the senators’ current proposal would rely too heavily on tests the companies could perform themselves.
The House has already left town until the week after the midterm elections. The Senate is poised to work this week and potentially next week before it breaks for the election.

Sen. John Kennedy of Louisiana, the only Republican who attended a closed-door briefing for lawmakers with AI specialists last week, tried to get unanimous consent to pass a “kill switch” bill last week — which would require AI companies to have an emergency shutoff — only for Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., to block it.
Kennedy was pessimistic that there would be any legislative action on AI in the lame duck session before 2027.

“We’re not going to do anything on AI this Congress,” he said in an interview. “I’m anxious to see what the president’s AI Force is going to look like and the details. But you’re not going to see this Congress do anything, in my opinion.”

title: U.S. and China agree to extend trade truce through Jan. 10, Bessent says
summary: The agreement extends the suspension of some tariffs as Chinese President Xi Jinping arrives in Washington for a state visit.
story: The United States and China have agreed to extend a bilateral trade truce that was set to expire in November through Jan. 10, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Wednesday.
The announcement came after Bessent and China’s vice premier, He Lifeng, held an unscheduled meeting in Washington.

“We will extend what we call the ‘Busan Agreement’ — the economic détente between the two countries that was scheduled to end on Nov. 10 — that is going to be extended until Jan. 10,” Bessent said in an interview on Fox News Channel.
Bessent said it’s possible a larger economic package will be agreed upon by January. But it’s also possible to “just roll the current deal” and extend it further.
Trump welcomes Xi at Joint Base Andrews

“There are some deliverables that have not been perfect on the Chinese side, so we also want to see, now that we’ve sat down and told them our expectations, if over the coming months they can be more fulsome in enacting the agreement,” he said.
The announcement, a big win for economic stability in both countries, came only minutes after Chinese President Xi Jinping touched down to begin a multiday state visit to Washington.

Bessent also indicated that there could be further announcements in coming days from the Chinese delegation, including agreements to buy more American agricultural products and potential deals in the financial services sector.
Since Sunday, Bessent and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer have been holding talks with their Chinese counterparts to lay the groundwork for the closely watched state visit.
On Sunday, Bessent and Greer announced that the U.S. and China had proposed exchanging alerts about AI-related hacking incidents, especially those that concern national security.
The U.S. and China could also agree on lists of goods on which lower tariffs would be applied as part of President Donald Trump’s “Board of Trade” initiative with China, Greer told reporters.

“We expect that the types of goods you’ll see in those lists are consumer goods, low-tech items coming in from the Chinese side,” he said. “On the U.S. side, energy products, agricultural goods, potentially medical devices and other things like that.”
Xi’s trip is his first state visit to the U.S. in more than a decade.

News of the trade truce extension is likely to be widely welcomed in Washington and Beijing, given that the U.S. and China are vital sources of goods for each other and for their millions of consumers and businesses.

title: CDC reports first measles death amid confusion over Pennsylvania cases
summary: The agency previously declined to recognize four measles-associated deaths the Pennsylvania Health Department reported over the last month.
story: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention acknowledged Wednesday that one measles death has occurred so far in 2026 but provided no clarity about who died or where.

The agency previously declined to recognize four measles-associated deaths the Pennsylvania Health Department reported over the last month. On Wednesday, the CDC’s measles outbreak page was updated to show one death with a note that the number “is subject to change” and that the agency will “update its reporting as additional information becomes available.”

The change left more questions than answers. The CDC declined to provide details about which death it was referring to or whether it occurred in Pennsylvania. The agency said its National Center for Health Statistics had verified that the death now posted on the CDC website had occurred and that measles had been listed as an underlying cause of death.

Two of the people whose deaths health officials reported in Pennsylvania were babies, including a newborn whose mother had measles while she was pregnant. One was a 40-year-old woman who had a history of asthma and severe lung disease, and another was an 18-year-old who developed a rare neurological condition that causes inflammation in the brain and spinal cord.
A Pennsylvania Health Department spokesperson said the department did not know which death the CDC was citing.

Pennsylvania’s Health Department considers a death to be “measles associated” if the person died within 30 days of showing symptoms and testing positive for the virus. It can also take into account people’s medical records and whether they were exposed to measles before they died.
The CDC’s website says it is working with the Council of State and Territorial Epidemiologists to “develop a standardized case definition for deaths due to measles.”
As of Wednesday, the CDC had confirmed 3,471 measles cases in 45 states and Washington, D.C., this year. More than 300 people have been hospitalized because of measles infection.
Three people died of measles in 2025: an adult in New Mexico and two young girls in Texas. The CDC readily acknowledged those deaths at the time based on information from state health departments.

On Wednesday, the Pennsylvania Health Department reported that its measles case count has soared to 835, with 111 cases in the last seven days. Two-thirds of those cases are in adults, and 164 people have been hospitalized in the state.

Nearly all people who have been diagnosed with measles are unvaccinated. Two doses of the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine are typically given around ages 1 and 5 and offer 97% protection against measles, usually for life. During measles outbreaks, babies as young as 6 months old can receive booster doses.

title: Federal authorities investigating attorney, accountant linked to Epstein’s estate, source says
summary: The lawyer, Darren Indyke, and the accountant, Richard Kahn, are administrators and executors of Jeffrey Epstein’s estate.
story: Federal authorities have opened an investigation into Jeffrey Epstein’s former attorney and accountant, a senior law enforcement official familiar with the probe told NBC News on Tuesday.
The lawyer, Darren Indyke, and the accountant, Richard Kahn, are administrators and executors of Epstein’s estate.
Interviews with witnesses have been ongoing, according to the law enforcement official, who could not confirm potential charges or allegations under review or a possible timeline for the case.

The Justice Department said in a statement that “we don’t comment on the existence, or lack thereof, of investigations. We have always said with regard to Epstein that if the evidence presents itself, we will investigate.”

Daniel Ruzumna, an attorney for Indyke and Kahn, said in a statement that the two had not been subpoenaed or asked to speak with federal prosecutors and have not been told they are the subjects or targets of any investigation. The focus and scope of the investigation were unclear, he said.
The Wall Street Journal first reported the probe.
Ruzumna said his clients are aware that federal prosecutors recently asked to speak with at least one person who “provided services” to Epstein.

He pointed to documents released in connection with the Epstein Files Transparency Act, which President Donald Trump signed last year, and said the documents showed that federal prosecutors did not consider Indyke and Kahn to be among Epstein’s potential co-conspirators during an investigation in 2018 and 2019.
Epstein died by suicide in 2019 at the Metropolitan Correctional Center in New York City, where he was jailed awaiting trial on sex trafficking charges.

The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York, which had been in the process of prosecuting Epstein when he died and secured a conviction against accomplice Ghislaine Maxwell, declined to comment.
Indyke and Kahn testified before the House Oversight Committee this year, Ruzumna said, and have given depositions in multiple lawsuits related to Epstein.

“Not a single individual has ever accused Mr. Indyke or Mr. Kahn of sexual abuse or trafficking, and they reject any suggestion that they were complicit in or in any way knowingly facilitated Mr. Epstein’s sexual abuse or trafficking — conduct that by all accounts occurred behind closed doors, in secluded locations, and at times when neither Mr. Indyke nor Mr. Kahn was present,” Ruzumna said.

Last week, the two men were named as defendants in their capacity as executors of his will in a lawsuit filed in federal court. Two women who say their photos were found in Epstein’s collection of sexually explicit images of children sued, saying they want Epstein’s estate to preserve and account for everything seized from his properties.

“We want a real, court-supervised process to identify and notify every survivor depicted in that collection,” said the attorney, Hillary Nappi. “Many of them have no idea their images exist in his files, and they deserve to know, and they deserve the chance to seek justice.”
An attorney for Indyke and Kahn said Wednesday that the lawsuit names them only in their capacity as co-executors of the Epstein estate, not as individuals.

title: Mystery men emerge from New York City sewers near Netanyahu’s hotel
summary: The NYPD insists there’s no threat to the prime minister or the United Nations.
story: Security cameras near a New York City hotel where Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was planning to stay captured three men emerging from sewers before dawn Wednesday, police said.
The appearance by the mysterious scavengers does not appear to be connected to Netanyahu or the ongoing United Nations General Assembly in Manhattan.

“We have seen a number of incidents over the past few months of individuals going into the sewer system to look for valuables and other scrap metal after a storm,” New York police said in a statement.

“This incident fits that same criteria, but out of an abundance of caution given the U.N. General Assembly and the sensitivity of the location, the NYPD is conducting additional security sweeps with our federal partners,” the police department said.
The three men popped out from the sewer at about 4:30 a.m. and left by car.
The police department has “a robust response to these incidents, which were deployed overnight and additional measures today,” police added.
It’s believed the men were behind similar incidents, mysteriously emerging from city sewers, captured on video this year.
The men, not affiliated with any public works crews, were seen climbing out of manholes in various Brooklyn neighborhoods in late May.

title: Why Republicans are leaning in on healthcare: From the Politics Desk
summary: Welcome to From the Politics Desk, a daily newsletter that brings you the NBC News Politics team’s latest reporting and analysis from the White House, Capitol Hill and the campaign trail.
story: Welcome to From the Politics Desk, a daily newsletter that brings you the NBC News Politics team’s latest reporting and analysis from the White House, Capitol Hill and the campaign trail.

In today’s edition, Sahil Kapur explores why Republicans on the campaign trail are highlighting healthcare, an issue that has been a political weakness for them. Plus, Alexander Smith explains what President Donald Trump’s Greenland deal really accomplishes.
— Adam Wollner
Why Republicans are leaning in on healthcare

Healthcare is shaping up to be a vulnerability for the GOP in the midterm elections: According to this month’s NBC News poll, registered voters nationally trust Democrats over Republicans on healthcare by 22 points. And a New York Times-Siena College poll similarly found that likely voters preferred Democrats by 24 points on the issue.

Still, Republicans are leaning in on the issue, with many of them using populist rhetoric criticizing insurance and drug companies. The goal, according to GOP strategists, is more about trying to narrow the Democratic advantage than expecting to win on healthcare.

In battleground Michigan, Senate candidate Mike Rogers released an ad inveighing against high prescription drug costs relative to Canada as he runs against Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, who backs “Medicare for All.”

In a New Jersey swing district, Republican Rep. Tom Kean Jr. is running an ad lamenting that too many families “suffer because of big insurance companies.” And even in deep red Kansas, Republican Sen. Roger Marshall has an ad that credits him for “standing up to big insurance.”

“Republicans need to make up a deficit with women voters, and when you ask women what they are most focused on, healthcare always scores very high,” said Republican pollster Bill McInturff, who co-conducts the NBC News poll with Democratic pollster Jeff Horwitt. He added: “You don’t have to win an issue. You just have to compete on the issue.”

But Democrats are blasting the $1 trillion in Medicaid spending cuts that Republicans passed on party lines in the “big, beautiful bill,” as well as a pot of Obamacare funding that Republicans successfully pushed to end last year.

According to NBC News polling, Democrats have consistently led on healthcare since the early 1990s. Their edge topped 30 points in 2008, ahead of a blue wave, and it fell to as little as 7 points in 2010, a red-wave year.

And while Republicans spent much of the last decade, including President Donald Trump’s first term, attempting to repeal or undo the Affordable Care Act, the party has never coalesced around an alternative. The party has long favored curtailing healthcare funding to align with its support for tax cuts, a position that is coming into conflict with its growing reliance on working-class voters.

Inside Trump’s Greenland deal: No invasion, a few compromises and the status quo

To hear President Donald Trump tell it, the deal he has sealed with Greenland and Denmark is “a dream come true” for the United States, allowing it to build more military bases on the vast Arctic island while restricting investment there by Russia and China.

The security pact falls short of Trump’s past expansionist demands, reaffirming Danish sovereignty over a land he previously said must become a U.S. territory, and respecting Greenlanders’ right to determine their own future.

Despite that, Trump wrote on Truth Social that the deal “gives the United States permanent control over security, and all other needs, in Greenland, completely addressing ALL of our many U.S. concerns.”

It’s the culmination of a yearslong fixation for Trump and a more recent push for control of the semiautonomous Danish territory, with his threats to use force if necessary alarming European allies and giving ammunition to the Kremlin as it continually tests Western cohesion and mettle.

While Denmark and Greenland have been eager to present the deal as a win for all sides, analysts have doubts about how much it actually improves on decades-old defense agreements — and how much was achieved through threats that couldn’t have been worked out through a more amicable diplomacy.

“This was a phenomenal amount of work to get to where we were already,” said William Alberque, a former NATO official who is now based in Berlin. “They just wanted to wave something in front of Trump and say, ‘You got more.’”

title: Walmart Deal Days sale is happening at the same time as fall Prime Day — here’s everything you should know
summary: Walmart’s Deal Day sale event is returning from Oct. 5 to 11. The sale will happen at the same time as Prime Big Deal Days, also known as October Prime Day, and will include sales on beauty products, TVs, holiday gifts and more.
story: Of all the sales Walmart has throughout the year, the most important ones happen in the summer and fall. In fact, this October, the retailer’s annual fall sale, Walmart Deal Days, is returning this year and will take place Oct. 5 to 11. The sale will overlap with Amazon’s Prime Big Deal Days, also referred to as October Prime Day or fall Prime, which is happening Oct. 6 and 7.

Walmart’s Deal Days sale will have up to 50% off home, kitchen, tech, skin care, toys and video games, entertainment, electronics and more. You’ll also find markdowns on brands like Apple, Dyson, Shark, Ninja, Beautiful by Drew Barrymore, Revlon, Coach, Mainstays, Samsung and many more. So if you’re shopping for a new television set, air fryer, bedding, hair care tool or holiday gifts ahead of Thanksgiving and Christmas, this is a great opportunity to do it. Even food items will be up to 30% off.

Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter.

Walmart’s Deal Days sale 2026 is happening Oct. 5 to 11, which overlaps with Amazon’s annual October Prime Day, which will take place Oct. 6 and 7. The Walmart deals will officially be live at 12 a.m. ET.

No, you don’t need a Walmart membership to shop deals from Walmart’s Deal Days sale. Though, those with a Walmart + membership typically get advanced access its sales, according to Walmart. A Walmart+ membership costs $12.95 a month ($98 a year), plus taxes.

As a home and kitchen editor and someone who cooks a lot myself, Beautiful by Drew Barrymore is one of my favorite kitchen appliance brands. title: How to store your air conditioner for the winter
summary: Removing your air conditioner from the window for winter can help prevent freezing temperatures and excess moisture from ruining it. HVAC experts share exactly how you should store it.
story: With all the content available online these days, it can be hard to figure out what’s real and what’s hype. While we don’t always have the answers, we have a direct line to people who do — which is why we present to you our series The Internet Made Me Ask, where we have experts break down the truth about some of the buzziest trends on our timelines, like whether jazz shoes are bad for your feet.

Fall has officially arrived, and with the cooler air (in most states) comes a fresh round of seasonal chores. Outdoor furniture gets covered up, sweaters come out of storage, and your window air conditioner needs to come out of the window. If that last task isn’t on your list, it should be.

According to Josh Mitchell, an HVAC technician and owner of Air Conditioner Lab, a site that helps consumers get information on HVAC issues, leaving your unit in place all winter can shorten its lifespan. But simply yanking it out and tucking it into a closet isn’t the answer either. Cleaning it and storing it the right way, Mitchell says, helps ensure it’s ready to perform when hot weather returns.
To help you take down, clean and store your air conditioner properly, I asked HVAC experts for their best advice. Here’s what they recommend.
When should you put your air conditioner in storage?

There’s no single right date for storing your AC unit; hot sleepers may want to hang on to theirs  a little longer, while those who get chilly at night may be ready to take it out sooner. Still, there’s a good benchmark you can follow.

“The general rule is that when the outdoor temperature continuously falls below 60 degrees Fahrenheit, you know it is time to turn off your air conditioner,” says Ben Green, an associate at The Chill Brothers, an HVAC service company in Texas. “You probably will not need the air conditioning once it gets that cool, and keeping it on could allow chilly drafts to enter your house.” Don’t wait for the first frost, either, Green adds, since freezing temperatures can damage the unit.
How to remove your air conditioner
Window air conditioners are bulky, heavy and awkward to maneuver, so taking one out can be a challenge. Once the unit is unplugged, these steps from Green can help make the job go more smoothly:

Remove the seals and weather stripping. Anything you used to keep the unit snug in the window can make it stick when you try to pull it out.Take off the brackets. Unscrew or unclip anything holding the unit in place.Tilt it slightly inward. As you lift it, angling the unit toward the room keeps leftover water from splashing back into your home.Watch the frame and sill. Lift carefully so the unit doesn’t bang into either one, which can cause damage to your AC and the window it’s in.Set it on a towel. Any remaining water will drip out, so let the towel catch it.
Remove the seals and weather stripping. Anything you used to keep the unit snug in the window can make it stick when you try to pull it out.
Take off the brackets. Unscrew or unclip anything holding the unit in place.
Tilt it slightly inward. As you lift it, angling the unit toward the room keeps leftover water from splashing back into your home.
Watch the frame and sill. Lift carefully so the unit doesn’t bang into either one, which can cause damage to your AC and the window it’s in.
Set it on a towel. Any remaining water will drip out, so let the towel catch it.
What products can you use to clean an air conditioner?

Below I share some tips on how to clean your air conditioner before you store it, so you’ll want to gather some of these cleaning supplies before you dive into the process. While you can certainly use a damp cloth and some soap and water, the experts I spoke with say there are also a handful of products on the market that can help you get the job done.

These soft, lint-free microfiber cloths are scratch-free and highly absorbent, making them a gentle way to clean delicate surfaces — including wiping down your air conditioner’s filter or the outside of the unit. Each cloth is machine washable, so it holds up to repeated use. The color-coded pack makes it easy to keep one cloth for your air conditioner and others for other jobs.

NBC Selected senior editor Shalwah Evans has them and she says she uses them to clean so many things around the home. “I wipe the dust from my air vents and furniture with these, not to mention they’re great for washing dishes and wiping windows and mirrors without leaving streaks and lint on glass,” she says.

Frost King’s foaming coil cleaner dissolves dirt, grease and oil from air conditioner coils, fan blades and reusable filters. The water-based formula is low-VOC, lemon-scented, needs no rinsing (just a simple wipe) and has a 360-degree valve that sprays at any angle to reach tight spots. It also helps neutralize odors from standing water in drain pans.

This gives you everything to restore an air conditioner’s coils and vents — including small brushes that slip between grates and firm-bristled brushes that work well on coils. There is also a curved brush that reaches deep inside the unit, scrubbing condenser fins without damaging the coils. It’s worth noting that while some dirt may come off if you use the brushes dry, using a bit of soap and water or a coil cleaner in conjunction with the brushes will allow them to be most effective.
How to clean your air conditioner before storing it

Once the unit is out of the window, give it a good cleaning before it goes into storage. It’s a key step for two reasons. “Dust and debris left on your air conditioner can reduce its efficiency when you go to restart it in the summer,” says Green. “Plus, if you put your AC away with water in it, mold could grow and nobody wants to inhale that when you turn it back on.”

The good news is that the job is relatively easy. “Simply wipe down the outside of it well and remember to clean or change the air filter,” says Green. If you see dirt on the coils, he adds, you can vacuum them or clean them lightly. Mitchell recommends washing the filter with a mild solution of soap and water. You can also use the products we mention above to ensure a thorough cleaning.
Finally, make sure everything is completely dry before you pack the unit away. Wipe down any spots that look damp, then let it sit in a cool, dry place until you’re certain no moisture remains.
How to store your air conditioner

Your AC is out of the window and clean, which means it’s finally ready to go into hibernation until warm weather returns. If you still have the original box, that’s the best place for it, says Green. No box? Wrap the unit in plastic instead. Either way, you’ll keep out dampness, dust and critters, he adds. Just make sure the unit sits upright, the same way it does in a window. “This is crucial because any residual fluids from tipping it could damage interior compartments,” says Green.

Next comes choosing the right spot. “Select a location that is dry and away from very hot or cold temperatures,” says Mitchell. “A garage, cellar, or even a closet are the ideal spaces. Just stay away from sheds and attics that could get extremely damp or cold in the winter. The worst thing for your unit is moisture, as it can cause rust and electrical damage.”
