title: Sunny Hostin reveals she was holdout juror in 1991 ‘Butcher of Tompkins Square Park’ trial
summary: Hostin said on “The View” that she changed her fellow jurors’ minds to find Daniel Rakowitz not criminally responsible by reason of insanity at his 1991 New York City trial.
story: “The View” host Sunny Hostin revealed that she was the holdout juror in the high-profile “Butcher of Tompkins Square Park” trial in 1991.
Hostin spoke about her time serving on that jury during a discussion about the Lindsay Clancy case, which ended this month in a mistrial with the jury split 11-1.

“The reason I felt that I feel so strongly about this holdout juror is because I was a holdout juror in a case, in the Daniel Rakowitz case,” Hostin said on Tuesday’s episode, to the shock of her castmates.

Rakowitz was accused of killing and dismembering Monika Beerle, a 26-year-old dance student, then boiling her body parts and feeding them in a soup to people in Tompkins Square Park in the East Village of Manhattan in 1989.
He was found not guilty by reason of insanity at his 1991 trial, which dominated headlines.
Hostin said she served on the jury before she went to law school.
“When I brought it up at the Hot Topics meeting, I don’t think everyone believed me. And then my producer looked it up, and I’m in The New York Times,” she said.

The show then aired a picture of a newspaper clipping from an old New York Times article that read: “Several jurors questioned afterward said one holdout juror was principally responsible for preventing them from returning a guilty verdict.”

“That was me,” Hostin said. “It was because I saw clearly that he was psychotic. He was in psychosis. He did not mean to kill her, and once he killed her, he panicked. He chopped up her body parts. Yes, boiled her body parts. Tried to commit the perfect crime ... and he fed her body parts to the unhoused.”
The jury deliberated for an intense nine days, and its talks were at times combative, Hostin recalled.

“One juror threw a chair at me they were so angry with me. But one by one I picked them off and said: ‘What about this? What about that?’ And we ended up all 12 unanimously voting that he was not criminally responsible by reason of insanity,” she said.
Rakowitz was ordered in 2010 to remain at maximum-security Kirby Forensic Psychiatric Center on Ward’s Island.
Hostin noted that Rakowitz remains in a mental institution, which she called “a different type of prison.”
Her castmates were stunned by Hostin’s revelation, some appearing to disagree with her position in the jury.
Co-host Alyssa Farah Griffin said, “And you got this guy off?” as Hostin described the grisly crime. Star Jones, who was seated next to Hostin, joked, “Excuse me, can I move over?”
Speaking about the Clancy case, Hostin called Massachusetts’ insanity defense “well-established” and said she agreed Clancy was not criminally responsible by reason of insanity.
Clancy’s defense argued she was not criminally responsible for killing her three children because she was suffering from postpartum psychosis.

Some jurors have said one holdout juror did not want to acquit. That juror, Michael P. Desronvil, spoke out last week, saying in a statement, “Based on all the physical evidence, key witnesses, and what the prosecution presented, I thought it was enough proof that she [Clancy] knew exactly what she was doing and planned.”

title: Harvey Weinstein sentenced to 15 years on New York sex crime conviction
summary: The former film producer pleaded not guilty and denies all allegations of nonconsensual sex.
story: Harvey Weinstein was sentenced to 15 years in prison Wednesday, more than a year after a jury found the former Hollywood mogul guilty of sexually assaulting former “Project Runway” production assistant Miriam Haley in a high-stakes retrial.
Weinstein appeared in the downtown Manhattan courtroom in a wheelchair, his hands cuffed to his seat.
In a victim impact statement read aloud in the courtroom, Haley said Weinstein “abused his position and power,” causing a “devastating effect on my life and security.”
“It is a life sentence for me,” Haley said.

Weinstein also addressed the court, again denying the allegations against him while apologizing to “anyone I may have hurt by my actions.” He had pleaded not guilty to a charge of first-degree criminal sexual act.
“I am not a perfect person,” he said, “but I am a person who has made mistakes.” He later added: “I am not a violent man.”

Judge Curtis Farber excoriated Weinstein before handing down his sentence. “You took what you wanted by force, and you have never accepted responsibility,” the judge told the former entertainment industry kingmaker.
Farber said Weinstein’s 15-year sentence will be followed by five years of supervised release and a requirement that he register as a sex offender.

Wednesday’s sentencing came after a protracted series of trials, appeals and courtroom proceedings that have kept Weinstein behind bars since his arrest in 2018, one of the key events of the #MeToo movement.

“Today was about the survivors,” Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg said in a statement, adding: “I’m moved, as we should all be moved, by their courage and their steadfastness through what has obviously been a challenging process.”
Six-year legal odyssey

Weinstein was originally convicted in 2020 of third-degree rape involving former aspiring actor Jessica Mann and first-degree criminal sexual act involving Haley. He was sentenced to 23 years in prison. But his conviction was overturned in 2024 by a New York state appeals court, and a judge ordered a new trial.

Weinstein was again found guilty in June 2025 of first-degree criminal sexual act involving Haley, who testified that he forcibly performed oral sex on her in his New York City apartment in 2006. The same jury acquitted him of a separate criminal sex act charge involving allegations from former model Kaja Sokola.

The jurors at Weinstein’s second New York trial could not reach a verdict on the charge related to Mann’s allegation, and a third trial on that charge also ended in a hung jury. In late June, prosecutors declined to try the Mann case a fourth time.

Weinstein was separately convicted in Los Angeles in December 2022 of rape and two counts of sexual assault related to a 2013 assault of an Italian actor and model. He was sentenced by a Los Angeles judge to 16 years in prison in February 2023.
He is set to be resentenced in L.A. after an appeals court vacated his original sentence.

The former producer and film distributor vehemently denies all allegations of sexual misconduct, insisting his sexual encounters were consensual. In all, more than 80 women have accused Weinstein of sexual assault or harassment.

Weinstein once lorded over Hollywood. Miramax, his first distribution label, released seminal independent films like “Clerks” and “Pulp Fiction.” He won an Oscar as a producer of “Shakespeare in Love.” In the early 2010s, his second distribution company scored back-to-back best picture wins for “The King’s Speech” and “The Artist.”

But his reign came crashing down in 2017 after The New York Times and The New Yorker published exposés detailing his alleged pattern of sexual harassment and assault. The first wave of accusations against him in 2017 propelled the #MeToo movement, a reckoning with sexual misconduct by powerful people in high-profile professions.

In recent years, Weinstein’s health has visibly declined, and he has faced various medical issues, including diagnoses of bone marrow cancer, kidney disease and diabetes. He has been held at the Bellevue Hospital prison ward, and he will remain there until he is sent to a state prison.

title: Over 100 people suffered brain injuries on X2 rollercoaster at Six Flags, victims’ lawyers say
summary: Three people say they sustained “catastrophic brain damage” on the California coaster and have sued the amusement park.
story: Three people who say they sustained “catastrophic” brain injuries riding the X2 roller coaster at Six Flags Magic Mountain in Southern California have sued the amusement park and the ride manufacturer for damages, court records show.

And, according to their lawyers, more than 100 other people also sustained brain injuries in the last two years riding what is billed as a roller coaster that “will have even the most hardened thrill seeker screaming.”

“These families, these people, went to Magic Mountain for some entertainment, for some family fun, and they suffered catastrophic brain damage,” attorney Gary Dordick said Tuesday at a news conference.

The lawsuits, filed Monday in California Superior Court, name as defendants Six Flags, several other people and S&S Worldwide, the manufacturer of the roller coaster. The injured riders are seeking unspecified damages.
Six Flags and S&S Worldwide did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The X2 has been closed since July 12, according to NBC Los Angeles.
“The design of this ride makes it inherently dangerous and makes it dangerous in a way that no reasonable rider would expect,” said attorney Christopher Bulone, who works with Dordick.
The X2 is a 200-foot-high roller coaster in Los Angeles County with rotating seats that spin as the ride twists and dives and flips along a track at speeds of up to 76 mph, according to Six Flags.
“Quite simply, you will be spun into another dimension,” the park promises.
Pamela Guillen was celebrating her daughter Camille Marquez’s 16th birthday at the park on July 5 when “she boarded X2 at her daughter’s urging.”
During the ride, Guillen repeatedly hit her head against the ride’s headrest, Dordick said.

“When X2 returned to the station, Camille looked at her mother and saw her sitting with a vacant stare and her mouth open,” the lawsuit says. “Camille initially thought Pamela was joking. She quickly realized that something was wrong.”

“Confused and unstable on her feet,” Guillen landed in the hospital, where surgeons had to remove part of her skull to treat her, and she did not regain consciousness for two weeks, according to the lawsuit.
Six Flags knew Guillen had been hurt but “continued to operate X2 without adequately investigating the cause of her injury or warning subsequent riders,” the lawsuit says.
And six days after Guillen was injured, Naomi Greer-Wilkinson, 25, “lost consciousness” after having ridden the X2 with her siblings on July 11.
Wilkinson underwent “multiple” operations to relieve the pressure on her brain but remains bedridden and barely conscious and is described in the court papers as “an incompetent adult.”

“Naomi had no idea, when she was going to Magic Mountain with her siblings and her friends, that she was signing up for something that could potentially rip the veins in her skull, cause catastrophic bleeding, and lead to a coma,” Bulone said.
The third lawsuit was filed on behalf of lawyer Michael Wilk, who said he was injured after he rode the X2 on Feb. 7.
“Michael’s head began slamming violently against the headrest of his seat,” the lawsuit says. “Immediately upon exiting the ride, Michael felt ill.”

In the weeks that followed, the suit says, Wilk’s co-workers noticed he was struggling and told him to see a doctor. An MRI examination revealed massive brain bleeding and swelling, according to the lawsuit.
Wilk underwent two operations to “relieve the pressure the bleeding was placing on his brain.”
Wilk, according to his lawsuit, can no longer practice law and “continues to suffer debilitating headaches, confusion, dizziness, memory loss and personality changes.”
Word of the lawsuits came in the wake of an investigation by CNN last month that documented at least two deaths and more than a dozen reports of serious injuries and hospitalizations by X2 riders.

title: Mystery men emerge from New York City sewers near Netanyahu’s hotel
summary: The NYPD insists there’s no threat to the prime minister or the United Nations.
story: Security cameras near a New York City hotel where Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was planning to stay captured three men emerging from sewers before dawn Wednesday, police said.
The appearance by the mysterious scavengers does not appear to be connected to Netanyahu or the ongoing United Nations General Assembly in Manhattan.

“We have seen a number of incidents over the past few months of individuals going into the sewer system to look for valuables and other scrap metal after a storm,” New York police said in a statement.

“This incident fits that same criteria, but out of an abundance of caution given the U.N. General Assembly and the sensitivity of the location, the NYPD is conducting additional security sweeps with our federal partners,” the police department said.
The three men popped out from the sewer at about 4:30 a.m. and left by car.
The police department has “a robust response to these incidents, which were deployed overnight and additional measures today,” police added.
It’s believed the men were behind similar incidents, mysteriously emerging from city sewers, captured on video this year.
The men, not affiliated with any public works crews, were seen climbing out of manholes in various Brooklyn neighborhoods in late May.

title: 61-Year-Old Singer Gets 4-Chair Turn and the Respect of Coaches on Final ‘The Voice’ Season 30 Premiere Night
summary: “The Voice” Season 30 kicked off with three episodes with singers joining either Team Adam Levine, Kelly Clarkson, Queen Latifah or Riley Green.
story: “The Voice” is back, the red chairs are turning and coaches are filling up their teams.
Season 30 of the NBC singing competition show kicked off on Monday, Sept. 21 with a two-hour premiere, followed by a second episode on Sept. 22.
Returning coaches Adam Levine, who won the previous season, and Kelly Clarkson welcomed Queen Latifah and Riley Green to the show as the Blind Auditions began.

During the first episode, host Carson Daly introduced the “First In Button,” which means that whichever coach turns first in a multi-chair turn has the chance to claim an artist before the artist’s final decision. They can only use this button once. Additionally, there are no blocks this season.

Also new is the “TikTok artist of the season.” All season long, the show will be tracking which contestants get the most likes and views on the show’s TikTok. The finalist with the most overall likes and shares will nab the title at the end of Season 30.
Check out “The Voice” Season 30 premiere highlights from the first and second episodes, including which coaches nabbed the first artists.
What Happened During ‘The Voice’ Season 30 Premiere?

During the Sept. 21 premiere, Queen Latifah was the first coach to land an artist on her team after a three-chair turn. Riley had a special moment singing his song “My Way” with a contestant, while Kelly offered up her hair extension to an artist so she could join her team.
A country-singing sister duo got the first four-chair turn of the night, and Queen Latifah used her “First In Button” to steal a singer from Kelly and Riley.
The “Worst Way” crooner also used his adorable pup Carl to convince a young star to join his team, but unfortunately it did not work.
The banter between the coaches kept the show feeling fun and flowing, as they poked fun at new coach Riley, his good looks and how he would win over the country singers.
What Happened During Night 2 of ‘The Voice’ Season 30 Premiere?
The Sept. 22 episode kicked off with Queen Latifah arriving on a motorcycle, impressing her fellow coaches.
The first singer of the night, 15-year-old Koumba Diallo, instantly impressed Queen Latifah after just one line. After receiving a four-chair turn, she had one tough decision to make.

Queen Latifah continued pulling out impressive stunts, including bringing backup singers to the stage when convincing an artist to join her team. (It worked!) Kelly also used her “First In” button to nab a soulful singer.
Adam, meanwhile, continued to be conservative with his chair turns, but a contestant singing a country song caught his attention. He, however, had to fight Riley for the aspiring star.

The episode ended with a cliffhanger after another four-chair turn got the coaches hyped. Adam and Kelly were making their best effort to nab  23-year-old Lexi Stephens from New York City, who they said could be the next winner.
Who did she choose? Viewers will find out on Night Three of “The Voice” Season 30 premiere week.
What Happened During Night 3 of ‘The Voice’ Season 30 Premiere?
The third episode began where it left off, with Lexi ultimately choosing Adam as her coach.

It was a special moment when 61-year-old Kyle Davis took a chance on continuing his singing dreams and auditioned for “The Voice.” Strumming along on his guitar, he received a four-chair turn that made him emotional.
There was also a powerhouse singer that Queen Latifah added to her team, while a tween captured the heart of Kelly.

After a stunning rendition of “Moon River” from Amanda Mikkel earned her a four-chair turn, it was her turn to choose a coach. Or was it? Eager to get her on their team, Adam went for it and used his “First In” button.

title: Nathan Fielder Releases Full Trailer for Elizabeth Holmes Doc. What to Know About ‘You Can See Everything’
summary: Director Nathan Fielder has released the full trailer for “You Can See Everything,” a doc about Elizabeth Holmes’ final days a free woman before she entered federal prison.
story: “Catch Me Up” is a TODAY series where our experts and journalists bring readers up to speed on the day’s biggest headlines.

After sharing an unsettling teaser from his upcoming documentary about Theranos founder and convicted felon Elizabeth Holmes, director Nathan Fielder has released the full trailer that shows the businesswoman still maintaining she did nothing wrong.
“You Can See Everything,” also from filmmaker Lance Oppenheim, follows Holmes during her final days as a free woman with partner Billy Evans and their children before she entered prison in 2023.
The trailer reveals that Fielder moved into Holmes’ house for the documentary.
“I think this is the moment in time to capture this story before I’m gone,” she seemingly tells the comedian at one point.
Evans is also featured. Fielder questions him in the clip about the start of his relationship with Holmes, asking Evans if he can truly trust her.
Even Fielder wonders if Holmes is being honest with him during their chats.
“That’s because I don’t have anything to hide,” she tells him as ominous music grows louder.

Just a few hours after Fielder shared the link for the trailer, it racked up over 2 million views on YouTube. Interest in “You Can See Everything,” out in theaters Oct. 16, has continued to grow since it had its worldwide premiere at a secret screening during the Telluride Film Festival.
Critics raved about the movie, which has a 100% on Rotten Tomatoes, and teased its unpredictability.
So, what can you expect from the buzzy documentary?
Rebecca Keegan of NBC News Digital was in attendance when “You Can See Everything” was screened Sept. 6 at the festival.
Read on to find out what she shared about the jaw-dropping reactions from those in the crowd.
What Happened at the ‘You Can See Everything’ Telluride Film Festival Screening?
“You Can See Everything” has gone viral since it was screened at the Telluride Film Festival earlier this month, with attendees having strong reactions.
“There were audible gasps and ‘no ways’ consistently throughout this almost three-hour film,” Keegan told NBC News correspondent Erin McLaughlin on TODAY Sept. 8.

Holmes was the founder and CEO of the tech startup Theranos, which promised to revolutionize blood testing. She was found guilty of four counts of wire fraud in January 2022 after a federal investigation uncovered critical violations in a Theranos lab following reports that the technology did not work and could deliver faulty results.
The new documentary features footage of Holmes with partner  Evans and their two children at a rental home in San Diego before Holmes’ sentence began. She is scheduled to be released in 2031.
“I think part of the film is exploring this question of Elizabeth Holmes’s perception of reality and about things that she’s done,” Keegan said.
The teaser trailer released by the studio A24 on Sept. 6 showed a wide-eyed Holmes awkwardly only inches away from Fielder’s face as she spoke to him in one scene.

“I’m not that person,” Holmes said in the clip. “I can promise you that. I don’t have anything to deceive you on. Of course, I’m not deceiving you. I’m engaging with you as a human being. Why would I deceive you? There’s no reason for me to do that.”
“OK. All right. OK, good chat,” Fielder replies.
The two then stare at each other for an uncomfortable duration.
“You’re being real right now?” Fielder asks.
“I’m always being real,” Holmes replies.
Keegan described the “strange feeling” produced by the interactions between Fielder and Holmes in the film.
“Fielder is very much a character in the film, and in some ways, it’s him trying to understand whether he believes Elizabeth Holmes or not,” Keegan said.

“I’m struggling to this day to understand exactly what I experienced,” Fielder said during the post-screening Q&A, according to Keegan. “I don’t know why they want me there. I’m a weird guy. I don’t get it. That messed with my head.”

The conversations between Holmes and “The Rehearsal” star are reportedly not the only surreal moments in the documentary. The film also includes an A-list Hollywood actor reenacting Fielder’s conversations with Holmes from prison. Fielder asked the attendees at the screening not to reveal the actor’s identity, according to Keegan.
NBC News reached out to Holmes for comment, but did not hear back. Holmes also shared the movie trailer on her X account on Sept. 6 and wrote, “I’m always being real.”

“You Can See Everything” is the latest screen adaptation of the saga involving Holmes. HBO released the documentary “The Inventor” about Holmes in 2019, and then Amanda Seyfried played her in the 2022 Hulu series “The Dropout.”

title: ‘Home Improvement’ Star Jonathan Taylor Thomas Detained for Obstruction and Public Intoxication
summary: Jonathan Taylor Thomas, best known as Randy Taylor on “Home Improvement,” was arrested for obstruction and public intoxication.
story: Jonathan Taylor Thomas, best known for playing Randy Taylor on “Home Improvement,” was arrested on Sept. 21, the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department confirmed.

The sheriff’s department told NBC News that the 45-year-old actor, whose given name is Jonathan Taylor Weiss, was detained after the car he was riding in was pulled over for a DUI investigation in the Westlake Village, California, area.

“Deputies saw a vehicle stopped at the intersection, with a green light blocking traffic. Deputies pulled alongside the vehicle to see if the driver needed assistance. Deputies noticed the driver was acting odd and appeared to be intoxicated,” the sheriff’s department told NBC News. “Deputies conducted a traffic stop on the vehicle for the violation and conducted a driving under the influence investigation.”

Thomas was a passenger in the car, according to authorities, and also appeared intoxicated. According to the sheriff’s department, while the sobriety tests were being performed on the driver, Thomas “continually exited the vehicle and approached the deputies, distracting them from their investigation.”
“Deputies attempted to detain (Thomas) for obstruction and public intoxication, at which point, (Thomas) kicked a deputy in the stomach,” the sheriff’s department said.

The actor was then arrested and taken to the Malibu/Lost Hills Sheriff’s Station where he was booked on the aforementioned felony charges, officials told NBC News. The driver of the vehicle was also arrested and booked for driving under the influence of alcohol.
According to jail records, Thomas was arrested at 1:50 a.m. on Monday, Sept. 21, and was released on Sept. 22 at 12 p.m.
Reps for Thomas did not immediately respond to TODAY.com’s request for comment.
The sheriff’s department said Thomas’ case will be submitted to the Ventura County District Attorney’s Office for filing consideration.

Thomas has kept out of the public eye for years, with his last acting credit being a 2015 appearance on Tim Allen’s show “Last Man Standing,” according to IMDb. He also directed a 2016 episode of the series.
Back in July, his former “Home Improvement” on-screen mom Patricia Richardson posted a photo with him and cast member Taran Noah Smith on Instagram.
Thomas, a ‘90s heartthrob, is also known for his roles in “Man of the House,” “Tom and Huck,” “Wild America” and “8 Simple Rules,” among others. He voiced young Simba in “The Lion King,” as well.

title: Who Is Bryan Seaver and What’s Happening With Dolly Parton’s Estate Lawsuit?
summary: Bryan Seaver, Dolly Parton’s nephew who announced her death to the world, is being sued by her estate management company for allegedly waging a “campaign of intimidation.”
story: “Catch Me Up” is a TODAY series where our journalists bring readers up to speed on the day’s biggest headlines. Here we uncover what to know about the lawsuit affecting the late Dolly Parton’s estate.
Many fans got to know Bryan Seaver, Dolly Parton’s nephew, after he was the one to announce the country icon’s death to the world in a heartfelt video shared on her official social media pages.

Weeks after Parton’s death, Seaver has reemerged in headlines for being at the center of a battle with the “Jolene” singer’s estate. On Sept. 22, She’s Alive, LLC, the entity that manages and protects the star’s professional property, business and more, filed a lawsuit and temporary restraining order against Seaver, claiming her nephew has engaged in an “escalating campaign of intimidation” against the entity, court documents say. The order was granted shortly after it was filed.
But who is Bryan Seaver and what does the lawsuit mean?
Who Is Bryan Seaver?

Seaver — the son of Dolly Parton’s sister Cassie Parton, one of her 11 siblings — served as the singer’s head of security for more than two decades. His professional security services stretch back to at least 2009, when he was credited as artist security for the country star on her television special “Dolly: Live in London O2 Arena,” according to his IMDB. He also had a small role in the star’s 1986 made-for-television musical film “A Smoky Mountain Christmas.”
In the video announcing her death, Seaver shared that Parton’s head of security role was previously fulfilled by his father Larry.

Currently, he serves as the CEO of the security firm Squadron Augmented Protection Services, which offers K9 services, event security and more in addition to estate security, according to his LinkedIn page.
Seaver and his services were terminated by She’s Alive on Sept. 16, according to the lawsuit filed by the estate management company, alleging Seaver made “escalating threats” against the entity.
In a statement sent to TMZ, Seaver and his team told the outlet that they were “dismayed” by the termination.

“We remain unshakably resolved to fulfill her final directive to protect her family, and we refuse to be intimidated by those whose actions we believe are being taken in bad faith and with the intent to profit from the life of someone who willingly gave so much,” they said in the statement.
Seaver did not immediately respond to NBC News’ request for comment.
What Was Bryan Seaver’s Relationship to Dolly Parton?

When it comes to his personal relationship with his aunt Dolly Parton, Seaver described himself as close with the country star. He said he was hand-picked by Parton to deliver the news of her death and shared Parton’s final wishes in the Aug. 25 video announcement of her passing.

“This video announcement is something Dolly asked of me years ago before I fully absorbed it as a future reality,” Seaver said, before calling the duty an “honor that is mixed with absolute pride and great sadness.”
Seaver also shared in the video that his touring experience started young, first joining Parton on the road as a child in the early 1980s.
“Dolly opened doors not just for me, but for her entire family to reach the potential we didn’t even know was possible,” he said.
What Does the Lawsuit Allege of Bryan Seaver?

The lawsuit brought by She’s Alive, which is spearheaded by Dolly Parton’s longtime manager Danny Nozell, claims that Seaver increasingly threatened violence and weaponized fear towards “those associated with Ms. Parton’s legacy” in an effort to inflict harm for “personal gain.”
Some of the alleged threats detailed in the lawsuit include one in which he reportedly said he was “going to set up a podcast dedicated to ruining Dolly’s Brand partnerships.”

She’s Alive also accused the former head of security of making “repeated, written threats” to the country star’s staff, partners, legal and business advisors and others. And due to Seaver’s previous claims of being a “former security operative with a military-contractor background,” many of those allegedly impacted by the threats are either afraid to come to work or have resigned entirely out of safety concerns, the lawsuit alleges.

“For example, in writing within just the past four weeks, Mr. Seaver has claimed to be ‘a killer,’ ‘an international arms dealer’ and a ‘mercenary,’” the lawsuit says. “He wrote, ‘All I do is warfare. Everyone needs to be worried about what I might do.’”
In another alleged instance mentioned in the lawsuit, Seaver wrote about his reported business dealings with Haiti on the day of Parton’s passing.
“I’m a killer,” Seaver wrote, according to the lawsuit. “I sold 27 million $ worth of ammunition and arms to the Haitian Police on the day Dolly died.”
The sequence of events, the lawsuit says, led She’s Alive to terminate Seaver’s services.

Through the lawsuit, the entity is seeking to block Seaver and his associates “permanently” from engaging in threatening behavior and intimidation tactics, ultimately prohibiting him from having any contact with the company or individuals involved in business with the estate.
The motion for a temporary restraining order against Seaver was filed and granted the same day.
What Has Bryan Seaver Said About The Allegations?

Seaver did not respond to NBC News’ request for comment on the allegations. In a text reported by the New York Times, Seaver said that his words were being misrepresented. He also said that he is carrying out his own investigation.

“This is a contrived out-of-context explanation of how this went down and it is being done in an effort to solidify me as some sort of opposition to her brand in her legacy,” Seaver told the outlet, “and that is not the case.”
The term “killer,” Seaver said, was one of endearment that Parton would use to describe him, he told the NYT.
“It was a joke we used around her camp,” he told the outlet. “I was her ‘baby boy ninja.’”

Seaver also said in message to the NYT that Nozell had been a longtime friend of his, and that some of the messages he had sent were about the pair’s efforts to keep others from exploiting Parton and her fortune.
“I trusted Danny,” Seaver told the outlet. “And that’s what those messages were, two friends and brothers commiserating on the people that have screwed Dolly over for many many years.”
Nozell did not immediately return NBC News’ request for comment.

title: Olivia Jade’s New Campaign References College Admissions Scandal — And Some Have Thoughts
summary: Social media users are split about Olivia Jade Giannulli’s Reformation collaboration, which pokes fun at the college admissions scheme involving her family.
story: “Catch Me Up” is a TODAY series where our experts and journalists bring readers up to speed on the day’s biggest headlines.
Olivia Jade Giannulli’s latest fashion collaboration is poking fun at her college admissions scandal, but some fans aren’t laughing.

On Sept. 16, fashion brand Reformation launched a new campaign with Giannulli, who goes by Olivia Jade online, with taglines and designs that reference the YouTuber’s past controversy. An email announcing the 26-year-old’s partnership with the brand showed her posing in a sweatshirt that read “College.”
“Since Olivia Jade is a Good Sport, we brought her back to campus for a lesson in getting dressed,” the brand said.

In 2019, Giannulli’s parents, Lori Loughlin and Mossimo Giannulli, were two of the most high-profile names linked to a college admissions scheme. Loughlin and Mossimo Giannulli were charged with paying fixers to get Olivia Jade Giannulli and sister Bella Giannulli into elite universities. The “Full House” star pleaded guilty to a federal charge of conspiracy to commit wire and mail fraud. She served two months in federal prison, paid a $150,000 fine and completed 100 hours of community service. Mossimo Giannulli, who also pleaded guilty, was sentenced to five months, 250 hours of community service and ordered to pay a $250,000 fine.

Read on to learn more about Olivia Jade Giannulli’s Reformation collaboration, including why some fans have said the photos are in poor taste and why others are calling it a “brilliant” marketing strategy.
Why Is Olivia Jade’s Reformation Ad Controversial?
Olivia Jade Giannulli stars in Reformation’s latest campaign that connects to her college admissions scandal.
For the photoshoot, the social media influencer posed in a “College” sweatshirt and snapped pictures on top of school desks in a classroom.
“@oliviajade is back on campus in a crew that suits her better than the other kind,” Reformation captioned the Instagram post announcing the collaboration.

The brand also shared that “100% of net proceeds” from the College Crew Olivia Jade Giannulli is sporting in some of the pictures will be donated to a nonprofit called Yes Scholars. The organization “identifies high-potential students from low-income communities in Los Angeles, New York City, and rural Appalachian North Carolina, and provides them with the long-term support, resources, and educational access required for success through high school, college, and career,” according to its website.
The crew appears to be another nod to the college controversy involving Olivia Jade Giannulli’s family.

Loughlin and Mossimo Giannulli previously admitted that they paid $500,000 to Rick Singer and Key Worldwide Foundation to help Olivia Jade Giannulli and Bella Giannulli get accepted into the University of Southern California by having them pretend to be rowing recruits. Federal investigators also said that the couple had their daughters pose for photos on rowing machines that were used in their admissions application.

title: Charles Spencer’s Book, ‘Swan Song’: Biggest Takeaways About Princess Diana
summary: What’s happening with Charles Spencer’s book, Swan Song? Here’s what to know and the biggest takeaways.
story: “Catch Me Up” is a TODAY series where our experts and journalists bring readers up to speed on the day’s biggest headlines.

The brother of the late Princess Diana has reignited the British royal drama surrounding her life and death with a new book giving his side of the story on her funeral, relationship with King Charles III and more.

Charles Spencer, 62, writes in “Swan Song” that his mother once told him he knew his sister Diana “better than anyone else in the world.” His aim is to “tell the truth about Diana, from her brother’s perspective.”
The allegations and remembrances in the book about Diana’s ex-husband, King Charles III, provoked a rare public response from Buckingham Palace.

“While we do not comment on books as a matter of principle, His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and color memory in ways others do not recognize, even many years after such a loss,” Buckingham Palace officials said in a statement on Sept. 16.

Diana was one of the most famous women in the world after marrying then-Prince Charles in 1981. Their high-profile marriage ended in 1996, and she died in a car crash in 1997 after being chased by paparazzi with her boyfriend Dodi Fayed. Fayed died, as did driver Henri Paul. Only bodyguard Trevor Rees-Jones survived.
Here’s what to know about Spencer’s claims and remembrances in “Swan Song.”
Prince Charles Said ‘We’ll Soon Forget’ Diana Ahead of Her Funeral

Spencer writes that then-Prince Charles made some ugly comments amid a dispute between the Spencers and the royal family over whether Diana’s children, Prince William and Prince Harry, should walk behind her coffin at her 1997 funeral.
Spencer thought it would be “barbaric,” but was told the boys’ father, Charles, wanted them to do it. Charles then angrily called him, Spencer writes.
“That’s the problem with your family, they’ve got no bloody sense of duty!” Spencer recalled Charles saying.
He writes that Charles then paused and unleashed “his horror that the world was so bowled over by her death.”
“Rest assured,’ he hissed, ‘we’ll forget her soon enough!’” Charles said about Diana.
“I can’t believe you just said that,” Spencer recalled saying.
Spencer writes that a palace official later called him and said the boys indicated that they wanted to walk behind their mother’s coffin, which was captured in memorable photos.
He Recalls His First Conversation with Prince Charles After Diana’s Death

Spencer writes that Prince Charles sounded “giddily elated,” in contrast to other callers, “who were stunned, barely able to articulate their condolences and offers of help.” Spencer remembers thinking his former brother-in-law sounded like a “lottery winner.”

“Looking back now, I suspect the prince’s first reaction must have been to think more of how this event might free him to marry the woman he loved, rather than appreciating the loss of one he did not. It can be hard to feel too much sympathy for an ex-spouse, or those who care for them profoundly, after bitter divorce,” he writes.
Charles went on to marry Camilla Parker Bowles, now Queen Camilla. Charles, in a 1994 interview, admitted to being unfaithful in his marriage to Diana.
Prince Charles Was Cruel to Diana About Her Weight and His Feelings For Her
Diana’s insecurities and body image issues were exacerbated by Charles, according to the book.
Spencer writes that just days after her engagement to the British royal in February 1981, Charles squeezed her waist and said, ‘Oh, a bit chubby here, aren’t we?”

He says his sister told him her waist shrank 5½ inches between her engagement and wedding. She confided in him that she had been suffering from an eating disorder for five months by her wedding day. The disorder was brought on by seeing her engagement photos.
Spencer later writes that Diana confided to a friend that Charles had told her “he was very happy to marry her, but he was not actually in love with her.”
Diana Said Charles Was ‘In Love With His Valet’
In a chapter about how Diana informed her brother that she was getting divorced from Charles, he tells her he fears the public will vilify her for ruining the fantasy of the royal marriage.
“But, Carlos, my husband is in love with his valet,’” he said Diana replied.
The valet is not specifically named. Spencer said he gulped in response.
“Well, I guess in that case, you don’t really have a choice,” he replied.
Diana Expressed Doubts About Her Wedding to Charles
Spencer recalls hearing that Diana went to their father, John Spencer, and said “she could not go through with marriage to a man who clearly did not love her.”
He said their father was “appalled” and “said it was impossible to pull out of such an enormous commitment at that point.”
Spencer described a subsequent birthday party for then-Prince Andrew in which Diana looked forward to reuniting with Prince Charles.
“But he had shown next to no interest in her, and she — deeply hurt, confused and increasingly concerned — danced with others, including me, instead,” he writes.
Charles Ranted About Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip Treating Him ‘Like a Child’
Spencer writes that he and Charles were standing “awkwardly” after the funeral for Spencer’s father when Charles blurted out, “You’re so lucky! You know, inheriting when you’re so young!”
Spencer writes that he had no idea how to react, as he was devastated by his father’s loss. Charles then expounded on his comment.

“You’re inheriting this place in your 20s. And, I mean, I’m 43,’ he said, ‘and I employ 50 people’ – he was flushed in the face now – ‘but my parents insist on treating me like – like a child!’ At this he stamped his foot in emphasis, I have to say, very much like a child; and a petulant one, at that.”
Diana Pushed Her Stepmother Down a Staircase
Spencer writes that he and his sister both “hated” their stepmother, Raine Spencer, whom their father, John Spencer, married in 1976.
Diana was “outraged” when she found out her father married Raine, while Charles considered her “a gold-digger.”

Diana’s dislike for her stepmother boiled over into a physical confrontation, according to the book. He said the two were at the top of a staircase in Althorp, home of the Spencer family, when Raine made a cutting remark.
“I have always felt so very sorry for the Prince of Wales, marrying somebody quite as stupid as you,” Raine said, according to Spencer.
Diana then “took a step forward, hooked a long leg round Raine’s calves before shoving her down the carpeted staircase.”
Spencer writes that his stepmother landed on her backside, got up, and left without a glance.
Spencer also writes that despite their fraught relationship for years, Diana and Raine seemed to form a “genuine friendship.”

title: ‘A Different World’ Stars Reveal the Surprising Romances That Happened Off Screen
summary: “A Different World” stars Cree Summer, Darryl M. Bell and Jasmine Guy remember Summer dating co-star Kadeem Hardison during the show’s run.
story: Viewers loved the romance between Whitley and Dwayne on “A Different World,” but it’s what was going on when the cameras weren’t rolling that may surprise fans.

Show stars Jasmine Guy, Cree Summer and Darryl M. Bell stopped by TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle on Sept. 23 to talk about the new Netflix reboot and reminisce about their time shooting the original sitcom, which included dishing about the real-life relationship happening off-camera.

“Whitley and Dwayne were that iconic couple that we all wanted to be, but we truly believe that you guys were dating,” guest co-host Justin Sylvester asked Guy of her co-star Kadeem Hardison. “You couldn’t tell me that that wasn’t real love. Was it behind the scenes? Did you guys have a little something something?”
“I do really love him, but he was seeing her,” Guy replied, pointing to Summer.
“In real life?” asked Sheinelle Jones. “You guys were dating? Why was I today years old when I found that out?”
Hardison, who plays Dwayne Wayne, and Summer dated while filming the show. Meanwhile, on-screen, Summer’s character, Freddie, started dating Ron Johnson, played by Bell, in Season 6.
“So I’m kissing Kadeem’s best friend,” Summer said, pointing to Bell.
“And Kadeem is kissing my best friend,” she added, pointing to Guy.
“Oh, that is just funny,” Sheinelle said.
“Very incestuous,” Summer added.
“Quite incestuous, yes,” said Guy.

The strangeness of the situation didn’t end there, though. Turns out, Guy’s boyfriend at the time, Dominic Hoffman, appeared in “A Different World” as one of Whitley’s love interests, Julian, who had a recurring role in the third and fourth seasons.
“Oh, it was messy over at Hillman!” Sylvester joked.
“It sounds very ‘Brady Bunch’-y,” Guy quipped.

“A Different World” aired for six seasons on NBC from 1987 until 1993. Enrollment at HBCUs increased more than 25% between 1976 and 1994, but the largest jump occurred between 1986 and 1994, according to the National Center for Education Statistics. That eight-year period is in lockstep with the show’s run.

“Every day, just like this, every day, one of us, someone will come and say, ‘I went to an HBCU because I watched “A Different World,”’ or ‘I went to college because I watched “A Different World.”’ ‘I’m a doctor,’ ‘I’m a lawyer,’ ‘I’m an engineer because I watched “A Different World,”’ Bell said.
“And then they’re like, ‘I found my Whitley or my Dwayne from “A Different World,”’ he continued. “It’s the gift that keeps on giving to us.”
The reboot of “A Different World” premieres on Netflix on Sept. 24, exactly 39 years to the day after the original comedy premiered on NBC.

title: Jon Hamm Opens Up About Becoming a Dad on TODAY, Including the 1 Thing He’s Most Excited About
summary: Jon Hamm and wife Anna Osceola are expecting their first child. The “Your Friends & Neighbors” co-stars married in June 2023.
story: Jon Hamm and wife Anna Osceola now have one additional outfit for their little one.

The former “Mad Men” star appeared on TODAY Sept. 23 to talk about his new series “American Hostage” on MGM+ in which he plays a radio host thrust into a crisis in 1977 when a hostage-taker  demands he take his call on air.
During his chat with Craig Melvin, Hamm also spoke about expecting his first child with Osceola.

“It’s great,” Hamm said. “The best thing I keep hearing is how much it changes you for the better. I’m very excited. I’ve been around kids my whole life. I’ve been a teacher, my nieces and nephews and all that stuff, so I’m excited to start our own family.
“And it’s thrilling. And terrifying.”
The couple are gathering all the essentials that their newborn will need, including plenty of onesies.
Now, they’ll have one more, as the anchors surprised Hamm with a special TODAY onesie in honor of Hamm’s professed love for Bravo programming and “The Real Housewives” franchise.
The special onesie reads, “Going to bed, so daddy can watch Bravo.”
“Beautiful,” Hamm said. “This will get used, I can tell you that much.”
Hamm also received a special message from Sonja Morgan, a former cast member of “The Real Housewives of New York City.”
The “Your Friends & Neighbors” co-stars were first rumored to be welcoming a child in August.
Hamm, 55, and Osceola, 38, tied the knot in June 2023.
The following year, Hamm opened up to The Hollywood Reporter about possibly starting a family with his new bride.
Hamm told the publication his parents’ divorce when he was young initially turned him off of the idea of marriage. But all that changed when he met Osceola.

“Obviously, my parents were not married long,” said Hamm, whose mom died when he was 10, “so I don’t have a model to look at and go, ‘Oh, this is how one finds happiness.’ I just knew at a certain point I wanted to be with this person. But when I proposed, I was terrified. I was like, ‘What am I doing?’”
The actor went on to say he and Osceola enjoyed a “perfect” wedding day in Big Sur at the same location the “Mad Men” finale was filmed nine years before.
The “emotional” event, he said, gave him “a reset, a reboot, a reframe, a reimagining.”
“So, it’s been great. And I hope it turns into kids. It’s not lost on me that I’m 53. I will be the old dad, but so it goes. It could be a good thing. We’ll see,” Hamm said.
Less than a year before getting hitched, Hamm opened up about his relationship with Osceola during a September 2022 interview on Howard Stern’s SiriusXM show.

“This is another place in my life that I feel very settled and comfortable. I’m in a relationship right now and ... it’s comfortable,” he said, adding, “It’s about taking care of someone else and being taken care of.”

Hamm revealed that after undergoing therapy to work on the “wound” of losing his mother at such a young age, he had become “opened up the possibility of things like being married, having kids, defining a new version of happiness, life, wellness.”
“It sounds hokey and whatever, but it’s real and for want of a better word, it’s what I’m working for. What else is there other than that?”

title: Frances Bean Cobain, 34, Makes Rare Red Carpet Appearance, Her First Since 2018
summary: Frances Bean Cobain made a rare public appearance when she attended a screening of the movie “The Deputy” in Los Angeles on Sept. 22.
story: Frances Bean Cobain made a rare public appearance when she attended a screening of the movie “The Deputy” in Los Angeles on Sept. 22.
It marked the first time the 34-year-old daughter of late Nirvana singer Kurt Cobain and Courtney Love had been photographed on a red carpet since 2018.
Cobain wore a brown leather jacket, which she paired with knee-high white boots, black shorts and a graphic T-shirt.
She is listed as an executive producer of “The Deputy,” according to IMDB. The film, which stars Duke Nicholson, William H. Macy and Tiffany Haddish, opens Sept. 25.

Cobain was last photographed at a public event in June 2019 when she attended the Moschino Spring/Summer 20 Menswear and Women’s Resort Collection show in Los Angeles. Her last red carpet appearance occurred at the Moschino x H&M fashion show in New York City in October 2018. Earlier that year, she was also photographed with Love at a concept store opening in Los Angeles.
Cobain and Riley Hawk, son of skateboarding legend Tony Hawk, married in October 2023, according to People. In September 2024, the couple welcomed a son named Ronin.
Cobain celebrated Ronin’s 2nd birthday earlier this month with a carousel of photos of him on Instagram.

“Happy 2nd birthday to this sweet potato fanatic, free wheeling, adrenaline seeking, nature loving, wind in the willows, sunshine boy!!” she wrote. “Once a day Riley & I look over at each other to say ‘I can’t believe we made him.’ I would live through every hard thing 1,000 times again, knowing it all lead to a present, loving life with this kid. Thank the universe he is here.”
Kurt Cobain died by suicide in 1994 when his daughter was 1. On the 30th anniversary of his death in 2024, she reflected on life without him.

“I wish I could’ve known my Dad. I wish I knew the cadence of his voice, how he liked his coffee or the way it felt to be tucked in after a bedtime story,” she wrote on Instagram. “I always wondered if he would’ve caught tadpoles with me during the muggy Washington summers, or if he smelled of Camel Lights & strawberry nesquik (his favorites, I’ve been told).

“But there is also deep wisdom being on an expedited path to understanding how precious life is. He gifted me a lesson in death that can only come through the LIVED experience of losing someone,” she continued. “It’s the gift of knowing for certain, when we love ourselves & those around us with compassion, with openness, with grace, the more meaningful our time here inherently becomes.”
She went on to reveal how she remained connected to him, decades after his death.
“Kurt wrote me a letter before I was born. The last line of it reads, ‘wherever you go or wherever I go, I will always be with you,’” she wrote.

“He kept this promise because he is present in so many ways. Whether it’s by hearing a song or through the hands we share, in those moments I get to spend a little time with my dad & he feels transcendent,” she added. “To anyone who has wondered what it would’ve looked like to live along side the people they have lost, I’m holding you in my thoughts today. The meaning of our grief is the same.”

title: Veronica Roth Shares First Chapter of New Novel Set in the World of ‘Divergent’
summary: Veronica Roth previews her new book set in the world of “Divergent,” called “The Sixth Faction.”
story: It is a truth universally acknowledged that a good story starts with a good first line. In TODAY’s “Cold Open,” authors tease their buzzy upcoming release by revealing and explaining its first line, paragraph or page.
Even Veronica Roth struggles to describes exactly what she’s doing with her new title, “The Sixth Faction.”
Is she rewriting “Divergent,” her breakout 2011 young adult dystopian novel? Is she crafting a brand new story? Is it an alternate universe?
“I think of it as a revisiting,” Roth tells TODAY.com.

“The Sixth Faction,” out Oct. 6, is set in the world of “Divergent,” where all of society is divided into five factions. When someone turns 16, they take an aptitude test that singles out the faction they would best fit into. The next day, they pick one in an annual Choosing Ceremony.

In “Divergent,” Beatrice Prior, later nicknamed Tris, grew up in Abnegation, the faction of the selfless, but learns through the test that she’s divergent, meaning she could excel in multiple factions. During her Choosing Ceremony, she picks Dauntless, defined by bravery, and begins its intense initiation process, through which she meets her eventual love interest Four.
That story was followed in two subsequent books, “Insurgent” and “Allegiant,” and three film adaptations, led by Shailene Woodley and Theo James.

“The Sixth Faction,” the first of a duology, will again find Beatrice on the precipice of Choosing Day. Per the book’s premise, she has a plan to choose Dauntless and leave her family in Abnegation, “but when tragedy strikes ... everything changes — her world, her plans, even Beatrice herself.”

“Writing these books was really helpful because it forced me to do two things,” Roth says. “One is to appreciate the original series, and the other is to observe the growth that I’ve gone through since I wrote those books.”
The first line of “The Sixth Faction” reads:
Our household’s mirror is behind a sliding panel in the wall upstairs, and I’m allowed to stand in front of it once every three months, when my mother cuts my hair.

Fans of the original books may find that familiar. “Divergent” similarly opens with a scene of Tris looking at her reflection as her hair is cut. But Roth wants readers to quickly understand: This Beatrice Prior has a different arc ahead of her.

“In the original series, she has a lot more uncertainty about what she’s going to decide,” Roth says. “In this one, I think you feel from the start that she knows that she’s got to go, then she changes her mind. So like how do we get there?”

Because “The Sixth Faction” follows Beatrice making a different choice, she realized she still needed to explore details about the larger world she lives in. So instead of one perspective, the book will follow three main characters — Beatrice, Four and Caleb, Beatrice’s brother.
“Caleb’s voice was very hard. I do not like innately understand that character,” Roth says. “I have to work at it, but I think the book is better for it.”

“The Sixth Faction” originally had a different beginning, Roth says, in which Beatrice steals a Dauntless shirt from a donation center and puts it on. “I liked it a lot, but she felt too ... she didn’t feel like herself.”
By starting the book in the same place as “Divergent,” Roth hopes to show, “this person is the same person, but has made slightly different calculations.”

She also teases that the “point of divergence” — pun intended — comes earlier in the narrative than people might think. “Divergent” and “The Sixth Faction” differ not just from the point Beatrice makes her choice, but from “deep in the world building, in the foundation of where the city comes from.”

“That’s how I think about it, I think about it as a multiverse. One exists completely independently of the other,” she says. “And I love the kind of puzzle part of this, where some of the same things will happen, but how do we get to them?”
Read the First Chapter of ‘The Sixth Faction’
Our household’s mirror is behind a sliding panel in the wall upstairs, and I’m allowed to stand in front of it once every three months, when my mother cuts my hair.

It’s the same choreography every time. I take the stool out of the hall closet and carry it over. She brings the scissors and the comb from the drawer in the bathroom. I sit. She slides the panel back. And I stare into my own eyes, hoping I’ll see something different this time.

But I’m the same. Small, pale. Bright blue eyes. Plain face. Dull blond hair. I want to keep staring, try on all my different expressions so I know what they look like. But even though I’m allowed to look at my reflection right now, I’m not supposed to revel in it. That would be vanity.
I look away.

My mother takes out the pins that are keeping my bun in place and then drags her fingers through my hair to unwind it. It would be easy to let this carry on the way it always has, this comforting ritual. But today I think of my brother, Caleb, how he’s been cutting his own hair for years, and my mother’s small smile and the tug of the comb make me feel like a child.
“Can I do it?” I ask her, nodding to the scissors.

She hesitates for only a moment before putting the scissors in my hand. I pinch my hair between two fingers the way I’ve seen her do it, and I think about shifting them higher, so I trim off more than just an inch. What if I cut my hair at my chin Could I be someone different then?
Don’t be ridiculous, I tell myself. A haircut doesn’t change a person.
But I’m just so desperate to be different. To be the person I’m supposed to be.
Desperate to be the person who fits here, in our faction, in our home, instead of the one who doesn’t.
I close the scissors over the first lock of hair, and cut.
Copyright © 2026 by Veronica Roth. Used with permission from HarperCollins Children’s Books.
Why Revisit ‘Divergent’?

Roth announced “The Sixth Faction” at BookCon in April, and at the time, she shared that part of the inspiration for “The Sixth Faction” was to release feelings of “negativity” she was still clinging to regarding the “Divergent” trilogy from critics.

“The anxious brain is like a sieve for negativity. So all the positivity flows directly through, and the sieve catches the negativity, thinking this must be honest because it’s uncomfortable,” she says.

She started the series when she was in college, and it published when she was 22. Looking back, she wishes she had taken more time between each new installment. But she rarely reflected on that time because of how much anxiety she felt during it.

Readers kept picking up the series, though, and she wanted to get to a point where she could be enthusiastic and “present” with the young readers on their journey with her books. Several things helped along the way. One, she went to Taylor Swift’s “Eras Tour” and watched Swift perform and celebrate songs dating all the way back to the beginning of her discography. And two, she listened to the audiobooks of the “Divergent” series and “had a much better time than I was expecting.”
“Then I started writing beginnings, like, can I get back into her voice?” she says. “And it took some time, but I did ultimately get into a good groove with it. ... It felt like going home.”
When she finally announced “The Sixth Faction,” she received plenty of big reactions. She remembers asking her husband if she’s handling the public pressure differently this time.
“He was like, ‘Yes, because you don’t fixate on other people’s opinions the way that you used to,’” she says.
She’s already written the second and final book in the new duology, titled “The Last Testimony” and due to publish in February 2027. That one, she admits, “was a lot harder” to write.

“I have a lot more baggage about the end of the ‘Divergent’ series than I do about the start,” she says. (The end of “Allegiant” is considered controversial to this day for reasons that are spoilers.)
“Every day was a little bit like remembering stuff that was a little harder to remember. But when I finished, I felt so much lighter,” she adds.
There’s one person in Roth’s life who was always thrilled by the project.
“My therapist was super excited by this project, by the way,” she says.

“I think writing my last book, ‘Seek the Traitor’s Son,’ was like a really fun outpouring of like joyful creativity. All the sci-fi, fantasy things I love were just crammed into one work, and that prepared me to write this book, because it’s like, just pursue the things that you like,” she adds. “That’s enough.”

title: Ina Garten Recalls the First Employee She Ever Fired — and the Hilarious Way It Backfired
summary: On an episode of Making Space, Hoda Kotb asks Ina Garten how she is successful while remaining kind. She shares a funny story that taught her a lesson about clarity.
story: When Ina Garten bought a small specialty food store called Barefoot Contessa on a whim, she knew nothing about running a business. Over the decades that followed, she built the store — and herself — into a household name, with bestselling cookbooks, hit Food Network shows and, most recently, a new podcast, “Happy Hour with Ina Garten.”
Garten is clearly a powerful, decisive businesswoman, but her public persona is one built on connection and warmth.

When the 78-year old sat down with Hoda Kotb for the September 23 episode of the “Making Space” podcast, Kotb points out that Garten has built an enormously successful career without appearing to “swing some sharp elbows” along the way. So how, she wondered, do you get to the top while remaining “sweet and kind”?
I think the two sides of me that seem diametrically opposed, which they’re really not, is kindness and clarity.
Ina Garten

“I think the two sides of me that seem diametrically opposed, which they’re really not, is kindness and generosity and warmth, but also clarity,” Garten replies. “Clarity can look tough, because I know what I want, and that’s what I want. And it doesn’t have to be mean.”
Garten says it was a lesson from her therapist, during her early days running Barefoot Contessa, that taught her how to strike that balance.

“I was running the store, and I was beside myself. I was just too exhausted. And [my therapist] said, ‘Your employees need two things from you: They need you to be clear and they need you to be happy.’”
But Garten admits clarity didn’t always come naturally to her — particularly when she first became a boss.

“I had to learn that.” she says. “The first person I fired was this sweet young woman. Oh my God, she was so sweet, and it was the first summer, and she was just terrible. And I took her out in the back, and I said, you know, maybe this isn’t the job for you, but maybe another job would be.”
Garten delivered the bad news so gently that her employee didn’t realize she’d been fired.

“The next day she showed up for work. I was so gentle; she didn’t know she was fired!” she recalls. “I let her stay for the rest of the summer because I couldn’t do it again. I already did it one time. I was so afraid I broke her spirit.”
Eventually, Garten learned that being kind and being clear aren’t opposites.
“If somebody’s not happy and not doing a good job, they know it. I would just convince them this isn’t the right job for them. But maybe [something else] would be a great job for them.”
Garten recalls sharing an office with her accountant at the time, who was often surprised by how employees reacted after Garten let them go.
“I would fire them, and then they would leave, and she’d go, ‘How did you do that? They thanked you when they left. What did you just say?’”
Her secret?
“We’re clear. We’re not tough. We’re clear,” she says.

title: Princess Diana Expressed Doubts About Her Wedding. This Family Member Stopped Her From Calling It Off
summary: Princess Diana expressed doubts over her wedding but was stopped by this close family member, her brother Charles Spencer writes in his memoir.
story: Before her famous royal wedding to the now King Charles III, Princess Diana expressed serious doubts about going through with the marriage, according to her brother.

In his new memoir “Swan Song: Diana, My Sister,” Diana’s younger brother, Charles Spencer, recalls learning that the princess had gone to their father, John Spencer, expressing that “she could not go through with marriage to a man who clearly did not love her.”
Diana and Charles were first linked in July 1980 and became engaged in February 1981.

Spencer details that Diana had attended the birthday party of Prince Andrew with her fiancé, whom she was very excited to be reunited with, as he had just returned that day from an official trip to New York. Andrew has since been stripped of his royal titles.

Spencer goes on to write, “Diana had dreamt of spending the party at Windsor Castle at her fiancé’s side. But he had shown next to no interest in her, and she — deeply hurt, confused and increasingly concerned — danced with others, including me, instead.”
Diana went to her father to share her feelings of uncertainty after that night. However, Charles Spencer says he didn’t find out the details of the conversation until much later.

Diana’s father, John Spencer, did not support her idea of ending the engagement. “My father was appalled and said it was impossible to pull out of such an enormous commitment at that point,” Spencer writes.
Spencer reflects on why he believes their father responded that way, pointing to his long connection to the royal family and sense of duty to the monarchy.
“He always adored Diana, but what she was proposing was counter to the code on which he had been brought up, and which he never seemed to question.”
Ending the engagement, Spencer says, would have meant “deeply embarrassing the Royal Family.”

Diana ultimately went through with the wedding, marrying Charles on July 29, 1981, at St. Paul’s Cathedral in London. Diana called the wedding “the worst day of my life,” in a series of recordings taped in 1991 for a biography titled, “Diana: Her True Story.”
Their marriage would eventually crumble, the royal pair separating in 1992 and finalizing their divorce in 1996, just a year before her death at 36.
Spencer’s account also notes a happier relationship that formed the night of Andrew’s birthday, when Elton John performed.
“The day after Prince Andrew’s party, with her usual impeccable manners, Diana wrote by hand to Elton John, her letter applauding him for his brilliance the previous night” he says.

Spencer says the exchange marked the beginning of a friendship that would continue throughout Diana’s life and ultimately became one of the most memorable moments at Diana’s funeral in 1997, when John performed a reworked version of “Candle in the Wind.”

title: Simone Biles Says Her Porsche Was Stolen After 3 Masked Intruders Broke Into Her Home: ‘Absolute Insanity’
summary: Simone Biles said three masked intruders stole her Porsche during a frightening break-in at a home she shared in Chicago with husband Jonathan Owens.
story: Simone Biles said three masked intruders stole her Porsche during a frightening break-in at a home she shared in Chicago with husband Jonathan Owens.
The legendary gymnast described what happened in a TikTok video on Sept. 21 in which she wrote in the caption that the luxury car has since been recovered.
Biles, 29, said in the video that she was getting ready to pick up her new car.

“Feel like I need a new car because during our last few months in Chicago, three men in masks came to our house and stole my Porsche,” she said. “Stole the GTS. But that’s another story. If you guys want to know, I’ll do a story time on that.”
Owens, 31, who is a safety for the Indianapolis Colts, previously played in Chicago for the Bears in 2024 and 2025. It’s not clear when the alleged burglary occurred.
“I feel like I need a reality TV show,” Biles said. “The things that happen to me are absolute insanity, and so it would be really easy for producers to just film regularly.”

Several high-profile athletes have been the victims of theft in recent years. A Seattle man was charged in 2025 for allegedly burglarizing the homes of multiple Seattle Mariners players as well as former Seattle Seahawks star Richard Sherman and Los Angeles Dodgers pitcher Blake Snell.
In 2024, the homes of Kansas City Chiefs stars Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce and Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow were burglarized.
Biles added that she and Owens have brought in additional protection after the car theft.
“That is one of the reasons why we also got our Doberman,” she said.

The revelation by the seven-time Olympic gold medalist came three months after she had a health scare she called “one of, if not the scariest experience of my life.” Biles shared the unspecified medical issue on her Instagram story on June 6.

“I’m not one to normally share things like this because I value privacy in today’s age,” Biles captioned a photo of her wrist with hospital bands on it. “But almost dying wasn’t on my bingo card earlier this week.”
Owens was in training camp with the Colts at the time.
“This was one of, if not the scariest experience of my life. Especially since Jonathan was in Indy for practices,” she wrote.
She then shared on her Instagram story on July 23 that she had a “procedure” that required a hospital visit.
Biles did specify what the procedure concerned or if it was connected to her health scare in June.

title: Taylor Swift Teases First New Song After Wedding: What We Know About ‘Patient Zero’
summary: Taylor Swift says she’s been “impatiently waiting” to share this new song with fans. The singer’s new song, “Patient Zero,” will be released on Sept. 25.
story: It’s a good day to be a Swiftie!
On Sept. 22, Taylor Swift announced that she is releasing a new song titled “Patient Zero” at the end of the week.
“I’ve been impatiently waiting to tell you that my brand new single ‘Patient Zero’ will be out on September 25 (!!!!!!!!!!!!)” the pop star wrote on her Instagram, alongside a new photo of herself.
The single is currently available to pre-order on Swift’s website for 24 hours.
The news comes after Swift has been leaving Easter eggs for fans the past two weeks, making Swifties question if the Grammy winner planned to announce new music.

Swifties first speculated that Swift was up to something when she appeared in a skit at the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards on Sept. 14. During the sketch, which featured cast members from “Law & Order: Special Victims Unit,” Swift looked directly into the camera and said, “Saccharide. Aries. From the Vineyard. North or South.”

Swifties immediately started to dissect the meaning, wondering if it pointed toward Swift releasing “Taylor’s Versions” of her debut and “Reputation” albums. For the past week, they have been sharing theories on social media.
One X user posted a tweet that unscrambled the phrase to seemingly reveal a hidden message: “My first record’s re-record is out Nov. 10.”
Then, fans noticed that a letter posted on Swift’s website in May 2025 confirming she purchased her master recordings suddenly  had three pages instead of two.
But theories linking the clues to her debut or “Reputation” albums started to lead to dead ends when zeroes began to appear in her song lyrics on Apple Music and Spotify.
The final piece of the puzzle? Swift updated her Instagram bio to read, “And, baby, that’s sh0w business f0r y0u” the same day a countdown appeared on her website.
All signs lead to “Patient Zero,” which will be Swift’s second release this year. In June, she announced the single “I Knew It, I Knew You,” from the “Toy Story 5” soundtrack.
Swift did not confirm if “Patient Zero” will be the lead single from her highly-anticipated 13th album.
Last year, she released “The Life of a Showgirl,” which included hits like “The Fate of Ophelia,” “Opalite” and “Elizabeth Taylor.”
Her 12th album broke a record with its first week sales, selling over 4 million units.

title: Who Was Nance O’Neil and Did She Really Have a Relationship with Lizzie Borden?
summary: Who was Nance O’Neil and did she really have a relationship with Lizzie Borden?
story: An unlikely friendship between a reclusive Lizzie Borden and an international actor is explored in the latest edition of the Netflix series “Monster.”

Borden, who was famously acquitted of murder charges in the hatchet deaths of her father and stepmother in 1893, was living in relative seclusion in 1904 when she met Nance O’Neil, a theater and silent film actor who had performed all over the world.
In “Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story,” O’Neil (Jessica Barden) appears in four episodes, including one about Borden’s life after her acquittal.
Here’s what to know about their friendship and how it’s portrayed in the Netflix series.
Who Was Nance O’Neil?
O’Neil was born Getrude Lamson in 1874 in California, according to her 1965 obituary in The New York Times.
Beginning her acting career at 19, she took the stage name Nance O’Neil in homage to English comedienne Nance Oldfield and tragedienne Eliza O’Neil.

O’Neil was hailed for her theater performances as tragic heroines and performed on “hundreds of stages around the world,” according to her obituary. She performed in the United States, New Zealand, Europe and Australia, drawing notice for her performances in Broadway plays like “The Passion Flower” and “The Lily,” according to Deadline.
She later transitioned to silent films, where she appeared in dozens of movies between 1913 and 1932, per Deadline.
How Did Nance O’Neil and Lizzie Borden Become Friends?
O’Neil was starring in a play in Boston in 1904 when she met Borden, who lived in nearby Fall River, Massachusetts.

After watching her perform, Borden sent O’Neil a bouquet of flowers expressing her admiration for O’Neil’s performance, the actor recalled an article by the New Bedford Standard following Borden’s death in 1927.
Their friendship “purportedly scandalized (Borden’s) more retiring sister,” Emma Borden, author Cara Robertson wrote in her book “The Trial of Lizzie Borden.”

Following her acquittal in the deaths of her parents in 1893, Borden had remained in her native Fall River but became a pariah. She “lived virtually alone” with “few if any close friends,” according to her 1927 obituary in The New York Times, making O’Neil one of the few who got to know her.
Following her notoriety from the trial, Borden tried to recast herself as “Lizbeth” instead of Lizzie, which Miller writes “may have been O’Neil’s influence.”

O’Neil was one of her few friends, but the relationship only lasted for a couple years. A 1905 story in the San Francisco Call reported O’Neil and her acting company giving a performance at Borden’s Massachusetts mansion named Maplecroft, where she lived with her sister, Emma Borden.

The story reports that O’Neil was an “intimate friend” of Borden’s who had met her a summer earlier at a resort near Boston. Their friendship lasted until O’Neil finished her theater season in the Northeast before she went on a national tour, according to the New Bedford Standard.

There were rumors of a romantic relationship between the two, but no definitive proof in any letters or writings by either woman. Their relationship was also dramatized in the 2010 theater production “Nance O’Neil.”
Borden never married, while O’Neil married British actor Arthur Hickman in 1916 and remained with him until his death in 1931.
O’Neil told the New Bedford Standard that Borden seemed “utterly lonely,” while noting that Borden’s notoriety for the murder trial did not matter to her.

“It did not alter our relations in the least,” she said. “Of course, the tragedy itself was never mentioned between us; never was there ever so much as an  allusion to it. I simply felt a great sympathy for her, and a great deal of admiration for the way she carried on.  She was always so alone.”

Borden, who secured a large inheritance following the death of her father and stepmother, may have helped out O’Neil financially. She helped her get out of debt to creditors and her manager, according to The Lizzie Borden House.
The two did not keep in touch after O’Neil resumed acting around the country and internationally.
“We were like ships that pass in the night and speak to each other in passing,” she told the New Bedford Standard.
How Is Their Friendship Portrayed in ‘Monster’?
Aspects of their friendship, real and imagined, appear in “Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story.”
Borden, played by Ella Beatty, is first shown seeing O’Neil onstage at a play in Boston.
“She’s enchanting,” Borden says.
After Borden greets O’Neil following the play, she asks her to dinner at her home.
O’Neil pops up in another episode in which she is shown imparting dramatic techniques to help Borden prepare for being on trial in the deaths of her father and stepmother.
It’s impossible for that sequence to have happened because the two didn’t meet until 1904, 12 years after the murders and 11 years after Borden’s acquittal.
In the final episode of the show, which details Borden’s life following her acquittal, Borden shows O’Neil the manicured landscaping and her menagerie of animals around her opulent Maplecroft estate.
O’Neil regales guests at dinner with her tales of performing in Europe, Egypt, Hawaii and Australia. The rumored financial relationship between Borden and O’Neil is also dramatized in the episode.
“Lizzie, it was your patronage that enabled all of it,” O’Neil tells her on the show. “Traveling first class, accommodation worth of a star, and I owe it all to you.”
O’Neil then talks about how she wants to leave the stage to do silent movies in the burgeoning motion picture industry. She also tries to hit up Borden for more money.
A rumored rift between Borden and her sister, Emma, over Borden’s friendship with O’Neil is also hinted at during a dramatic scene at dinner.
Emma Borden, played by Billie Lourd, castigates her sister in front of her dinner guests while calling O’Neil a “pig-s--- actress.”
Emma Borden never spoke about the reason for her rift with her sister in their later years that caused Emma to move out in 1905, so there’s no record that it was caused by O’Neil.

“The happenings in the French Street house that caused me to leave I must refuse to talk about. I did not go until conditions became absolutely unbearable,” Emma Borden said, according to Lizzie Borden’s obituary.

title: ‘The West Wing’ Turns 27: See Rob Lowe Explain the NBC Drama’s Success in 2000 TODAY Interview
summary: In 2000, Rob Lowe spoke with TODAY about what it was like working on “The West Wing” and why the show took steps to be as realistic as possible.
story: Welcome to the “TODAY Archives,” where we revisit memories from our show when celebrities and newsmakers started discourse, made us laugh or shaped our culture. This latest installment highlights Rob Lowe talking about “The West Wing” on Feb. 18, 2000, during its first season.
“The West Wing” shot out of a cannon when it premiered on Sept. 22, 1999. The NBC drama, about Martin Sheen’s fictional President Jed Bartlet and his staff, was a ratings hit and critical success.

Rob Lowe portrayed Sam Seaborn, the White House deputy communications director, a role he played from the premiere until the fourth season, before returning for an appearance in the show’s seventh and final season. Lowe visited TODAY on Feb. 18, 2000 to chat with Katie Couric about the heavily-hyped series, which would net him an Emmy nomination in 2001.
“The West Wing” won best drama series at the Emmys in 2000, the first of four consecutive years it would collect the award.
“It’s got the buzz,” Couric said about the series.
“I’m so excited. We worked so hard to do it, and to have people just embrace it in the way that they have is, it’s gratifying, and it keeps us really pumped up,” Lowe said.
What Did Then-President Bill Clinton Think About ‘The West Wing’?
Lowe said President Bill Clinton, who was in office when the show premiered, was all for it.
“I had the honor of going to the White House for the first time, and I met the president, President Clinton, and he said, ‘Tell President Sheen, I approve,’” Lowe said in a Clinton voice.
Lowe said Clinton’s staff watched the show, adding that White House personnel told him they felt “The West Wing” did an accurate job depicting life at 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue.
